docs.title: Approved principles
docs.text:
• Registration, licensing and capacity validation are separate states.
  • Commercial rights are central entitlements; executable permissions are device-bound signed grants.
  • Customer rights may be pooled and reallocated, while grants remain device-bound.
  • The same trust model supports online, assisted-offline and fully air-gapped operation.
  • Marketplace and OTA live inside LMS because they use the same customer, device, entitlement, capacity and release data.
  • Automatic updates consume Stable releases by default; LTS is explicitly controlled by the company.
  • Model files are independently versioned, encrypted, signed, inventory-aware and rollback-capable.
  • Capacity assessment recommends feasible deployment and never silently reduces purchased rights.

docs.text:
# ADR-XXX — Title

Status: Proposed | Approved | Open Decision | Deprecated
Date: YYYY-MM-DD

## Context
## Decision
## Alternatives Considered
## Consequences
## Security / Operational Impact
## Follow-up

Approved ADRs may only be superseded by a newer ADR; do not silently rewrite historical decisions.

docs.title: ADR-001 — Digitally Signed Device-Bound Grants
docs.text: Status: Approved Decision class: Security / Licensing Scope: Central LMS + Edge License Agent

docs.title: Context
docs.text: LMS must authorize feature execution on connected, intermittently connected and fully air-gapped devices. A central database lookup alone cannot authorize offline runtime, and reusable license files would be vulnerable to copying between devices.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Use centrally issued, digitally signed, device-bound grants as the executable authorization artifact.

A grant SHALL include subject identity, capability/limits, commercial validity, offline/grace policy, revision/supersession, dependencies and signing metadata. The device verifies the grant using a trusted public key before runtime use.

Production signing private keys remain outside normal LMS application/database storage.

docs.title: Central online lookup only
docs.text: Rejected because air-gapped/offline operation is a first-class requirement.

docs.title: Unsigned local license files
docs.text: Rejected because tampering cannot be reliably detected.

docs.title: Customer-wide reusable license key/file
docs.text: Rejected because it increases cloning/reuse risk and weakens device-level allocation/revocation.

docs.title: Positive
docs.text:
• offline verification works without central connectivity
  • tampering/forgery is detectable
  • device-specific quantities and dependencies can be enforced
  • supersession/revision supports controlled renewal/reallocation

docs.title: Negative / cost
docs.text:
• key custody, rotation and trust-store management are required
  • offline revocation is delayed until import/expiry
  • compromised root access on the edge remains outside full software control

docs.title: Security / operational impact
docs.text:
• grant verification fails closed
  • devices persist highest accepted revision
  • signing outage blocks new issuance but not already-valid grants
  • support must distinguish issued, delivered and accepted states

docs.title: Related requirements
docs.text: SDR-LIC-004, SDR-LIC-007, SDR-LIC-008, SDR-SEC-003, SDR-SEC-004

docs.title: Follow-up
docs.text: Grant canonicalization and exact wire format are finalized in implementation/OpenAPI/schema work without changing this decision.

docs.title: ADR-002 — Modular Monolith First
docs.text: Status: Approved Decision class: Backend Architecture

docs.title: Context
docs.text: LMS spans registry, licensing, policy, capacity, marketplace, release, offline workflows, renewals, integrations and audit. Early microservice decomposition would add distributed transactions, deployment overhead and operational complexity before scale boundaries are proven.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Implement the central Python/FastAPI platform as a modular monolith with explicit domain/module ownership and service interfaces.

Modules share one deployable process and PostgreSQL database initially but SHALL maintain clear internal boundaries so later extraction remains possible.

docs.title: Microservices from day one
docs.text: Rejected due to premature operational complexity, cross-service consistency risk and slower delivery.

docs.title: Unstructured monolith
docs.text: Rejected because domain boundaries would erode and future extraction/testing would be harder.

docs.title: Positive
docs.text:
• simpler deployment/observability/transactions
  • faster cross-domain iteration
  • easier customer-hosted packaging
  • strong transactional consistency for entitlement/allocation/grant workflows

docs.title: Negative / risk
docs.text:
• discipline is required to prevent module coupling
  • scaling is process/database oriented initially
  • module boundaries are architectural rather than infrastructure-enforced

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• controllers do not directly orchestrate unrelated modules
  • cross-module actions use application/use-case services
  • module ownership of tables/services/endpoints is documented
  • internal events/outbox are used for asynchronous external side effects
  • future extraction must preserve contracts rather than copy hidden dependencies

docs.title: Related requirements
docs.text: SDR-PLT-003, SDR-BE-003, SDR-BE-004

docs.title: ADR-003 — Marketplace and OTA Remain Inside LMS
docs.text: Status: Approved Decision class: Product / Platform Architecture

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Feature discovery, trial/purchase eligibility, compatibility, capacity preview, release selection and deployment all depend on the same customer, device, entitlement, policy, capacity and audit data.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Marketplace and OTA SHALL be distinct logical modules within LMS rather than separate standalone products in the initial architecture.

Artifact storage may use an external repository, and delivery infrastructure may later be extracted, but business eligibility and orchestration remain governed by LMS.

docs.title: Separate Marketplace service/application
docs.text: Rejected initially because it would duplicate customer/device/entitlement state and create synchronization complexity.

docs.title: Separate OTA control plane
docs.text: Rejected initially because release eligibility, update rights and device lifecycle already live in LMS.

docs.title: Positive
docs.text:
• one source of truth for eligibility and device state
  • easier trial/purchase-to-deployment flow
  • common audit and authorization model
  • reduced duplicated integration logic

docs.title: Negative / risk
docs.text:
• LMS has broader scope
  • strong internal module boundaries are required
  • scaling of artifact transfer must remain separated from transactional API concerns

docs.title: Related requirements
docs.text: SDR-MKT-001 through SDR-MKT-005, SDR-OTA-*

docs.title: ADR-004 — Traditional Signed Edge Release Packages
docs.text: Status: Approved Decision class: Edge / Release Architecture

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Target deployments include Linux edge devices today and future Windows-compatible environments. Some customer sites are offline/air-gapped. Requiring Docker/container runtime on every edge host would constrain supported environments and add operational dependencies.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Edge application delivery SHALL use manifest-driven traditional signed release packages rather than making Docker a platform dependency.

Packages include signed metadata plus application/UI/dependency/config/migration/install/rollback/health artifacts. Linux handlers are implemented first; interfaces remain compatible with future Windows-native handlers.

Models remain independently versioned/encrypted artifacts and may be coordinated through a Release Set.

docs.title: Docker-only edge deployment
docs.text: Rejected because it would narrow target environments and complicate some customer-hosted/Windows/offline use cases.

docs.title: Manual file-copy installers
docs.text: Rejected because they do not provide deterministic verification, migration, health and rollback semantics.

docs.title: Positive
docs.text:
• works in constrained/offline environments
  • no container runtime dependency
  • package can carry deterministic migration/health/rollback logic
  • future Windows packaging remains feasible

docs.title: Negative / risk
docs.text:
• installer/update manager must handle OS differences explicitly
  • package format/security is more responsibility for LMS/edge team
  • script execution must be tightly constrained

docs.title: Related requirements
docs.text: SDR-PLT-004, SDR-PLT-005, SDR-OTA-006 through SDR-OTA-010

docs.title: Follow-up
docs.text: ADR-010 freezes the exact archive/handler format before Update Manager implementation freeze.

docs.title: ADR-005 — Device-Generated Cryptographic Identity
docs.text: Status: Approved Decision class: Security / Device Lifecycle

docs.title: Context
docs.text: MAC address, hostname or a customer-shared activation code can be copied/spoofed and are insufficient for device-bound grants. Hardware can also change legitimately over device lifetime.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Each device SHALL generate/hold an asymmetric key pair and register its public key with LMS. A versioned weighted hardware fingerprint is supporting identity evidence; MAC/network identifiers are evidence only.

Minor hardware changes are tolerated according to fingerprint policy. Major identity change, key loss or motherboard-level change enters REHOST_REQUIRED and requires controlled approval.

docs.title: MAC-address identity
docs.text: Rejected because MACs are mutable/spoofable and unreliable across replacements.

docs.title: Server-generated shared device secret
docs.text: Rejected because centralized secret distribution increases cloning/custody risk.

docs.title: Exact immutable hardware hash
docs.text: Rejected because legitimate RAM/storage/NIC changes would unnecessarily invalidate devices.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• grants/offline requests can bind to a cryptographic principal
  • cloning becomes harder than copying a license file
  • key storage quality on the edge matters
  • rehost/transfer workflows become explicit business/security processes
  • hardware fingerprint algorithm must be versioned and testable

docs.title: Related requirements
docs.text: SDR-DEV-005 through SDR-DEV-010

docs.title: ADR-006 — Separate License and Release Signing Keys
docs.text: Status: Approved Decision class: Security / Cryptographic Architecture

docs.title: Context
docs.text: License grants and software/model releases represent different trust purposes. Reusing one signing key would increase blast radius and make rotation/incident handling ambiguous.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Use separate cryptographic key purposes and key identities for license/grant signing and software/model release signing. Additional separation for model/key-wrapping operations MAY be introduced without changing this ADR.

docs.title: One platform-wide signing key
docs.text: Rejected because compromise, rotation and authorization policy would affect unrelated trust domains.

docs.title: Application-stored private keys
docs.text: Rejected because normal application/database compromise would become signing compromise.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• reduced compromise blast radius
  • independent rotation/recovery windows
  • distinct authorization policy for signing requests
  • devices must trust/version multiple public-key purposes
  • audit records must include key purpose and key ID

docs.title: Security / operational impact
docs.text: Production private keys remain in KMS/HSM/equivalent protected provider. Trust-store distribution must support overlap between active and retiring verification keys.

docs.title: Related requirements
docs.text: SDR-SEC-003, SDR-SEC-004, SDR-MOD-002

docs.title: ADR-007 — Signed Offline Request/Response
docs.text: Status: Approved

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Offline/air-gapped workflows use device-bound signed requests and centrally issued signed response packages linked by request ID and nonce. Relay devices are transport-only.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: The same trust model works online and offline while limiting replay and preventing relay workstations from becoming signing authorities.

docs.title: ADR-008 — Production Human Authentication
docs.text: Status: Open Decision

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Development begins with username/password. Production enterprise deployments may require OIDC/SSO, MFA and customer identity-provider integration.

docs.title: Decision required
docs.text: Select the production authentication profile and deployment-specific identity-provider integration model before production readiness freeze. Authorization/RBAC is designed independently so the decision does not rewrite domain permissions.

docs.title: ADR-009 — Model Encryption and Key Wrapping
docs.text: Status: Open Security Decision

docs.title: Baseline
docs.text: Model artifacts are encrypted and signed. Entitlement controls authorization and device identity controls whether content-key material may be unwrapped/used.

docs.title: Decision required
docs.text: Finalize envelope-encryption algorithm, key hierarchy, KMS/HSM integration, per-device/per-deployment wrapping strategy, edge secure-storage expectations and rotation/recovery procedure. A universal model password is prohibited.

docs.title: ADR-010 — Release Package Format
docs.text: Status: Proposed

docs.title: Baseline
docs.text: Traditional release bundle with signed manifest, application/UI/dependency artifacts, automated migration, health-check and rollback handlers. Linux shell handlers are first; Windows PowerShell equivalents remain future-compatible.

docs.title: Decision required
docs.text: Freeze archive/container format, canonical manifest serialization, compression, maximum package size, script execution sandboxing and artifact repository layout before Update Manager implementation is finalized.

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text:
The LMS is a modular enterprise control plane. Business truth is centralized; final authorization and installation enforcement remain local.

flowchart TB
    P[Admin / Customer Portal] --> API[Central LMS API]
    API --> REG[Registry & Enrollment]
    API --> ENT[Entitlement Engine]
    API --> POL[Policy Engine]
    API --> CAP[Capacity Service]
    API --> MKT[Marketplace]
    API --> REL[Release / OTA]
    API --> LIFE[Lifecycle / Renewal]
    API --> AUD[Audit & Reporting]
    ENT --> SIGN[Protected Signing Service]
    POL --> SIGN
    REL --> AR[(Artifact Repository)]
    API --> DB[(PostgreSQL)]
    API -->|Online| EDGE[Edge / Server]
    API -->|Signed request-response| RELAY[Authorized Relay]
    RELAY --> EDGE
    EDGE --> ID[Device Identity]
    EDGE --> LA[License Agent]
    EDGE --> LC[Local Capacity Engine]
    EDGE --> UM[Update Manager]
    EDGE --> RT[Analytics Runtime]

docs.title: Responsibility split
docs.text:
• Entitlement Engine: what the customer owns.
  • Policy Engine: under what conditions it may be used.
  • Capacity Engine: what the hardware can run safely.
  • Release/OTA: which software/model artifacts are installed.
  • License Agent: whether the feature may execute.

docs.title: Artifact Storage Architecture
docs.text: PostgreSQL stores transactional metadata, references, hashes, signatures, compatibility and deployment state. Large application/model binaries must not be stored as normal PostgreSQL blobs.

docs.title: Storage abstraction
docs.text:
Release / Model Service
        ↓
Artifact Repository Interface
        ├── SaaS: S3-compatible object storage
        └── Customer-hosted: MinIO or approved local repository

docs.title: Stored metadata
docs.text: Database records include artifact ID, release/model association, URI/reference, size, content hash, signature/key ID, encryption profile, creation/publish state and retention metadata.

docs.title: Integrity
docs.text: Artifact bytes are immutable after publication. Replacement requires a new artifact/release identity. The edge verifies manifest signature and content hash before installation/decryption.

docs.title: Signing separation
docs.text: Artifact storage is not a signing authority. Signing keys remain in the protected signing boundary; the repository stores only signed outputs and verification metadata.

docs.title: Configuration & Policy Hierarchy
docs.text: The platform must resolve configuration deterministically across platform, product, customer, site and device scopes.

docs.title: Resolution order
docs.text:
Platform Default
    ↓
Product Override
    ↓
Customer / Entitlement Override
    ↓
Site Override
    ↓
Device Override

Only explicitly allowed policy keys may be overridden at lower scopes. Security minimums may be marked non-relaxable.

docs.title: Policy domains
docs.text:
• offline authorization duration
  • grace duration
  • trial duration and eligibility
  • release channel eligibility
  • automatic/manual OTA mode
  • maintenance window
  • rollback behavior
  • model-only update permission
  • concurrency limits
  • notification preferences
  • audit retention
  • capacity override policy

docs.title: Example resolved policy
docs.text:
{
  "offline_days": 7,
  "grace_days": 7,
  "trial_days": 14,
  "ota_mode": "auto",
  "release_channel": "stable",
  "maintenance_window": {"start": "01:00", "end": "03:00", "timezone": "site"},
  "auto_rollback": true,
  "model_only_updates": true
}

docs.title: Governance
docs.text: Every resolved policy response should include source metadata so operators can see which scope supplied each effective value. Changes to sensitive policy keys are audited.

docs.title: Deployment Models
docs.text: The same LMS application architecture supports SaaS and customer-hosted deployments with configuration/provider adapters rather than separate product forks.

docs.title: SaaS baseline
docs.text:
• multi-tenant logical isolation
  • Phase 1 single-primary application/database baseline
  • automated encrypted backups and tested restore
  • externalized artifact repository
  • protected signing provider
  • health monitoring and alerting
  • design remains horizontally/HA evolvable without changing domain model

docs.title: Customer-hosted baseline
docs.text:
• same application codebase
  • isolated customer deployment
  • customer-managed or vendor-approved PostgreSQL/artifact storage/signing integration
  • manual signed LMS upgrade package initially
  • outbound dependencies minimized and explicitly documented
  • HA optional enterprise deployment profile
  • customer environment may be disconnected from vendor SaaS

docs.title: Edge connectivity modes
docs.text:
1. Online — device communicates directly with LMS.
  2. Assisted offline — authorized relay transports signed request/response data.
  3. Fully air-gapped — controlled media carries signed request/response packages.

All routes use the same grant/artifact trust model; connectivity mode changes transport, not authorization semantics.

docs.title: Deployment dependencies
docs.text: Dependency SaaS Customer-hosted Failure effect PostgreSQL vendor managed customer/vendor managed LMS writes unavailable; no unsigned fallback Artifact storage object storage MinIO/approved repository package delivery unavailable Signing provider KMS/HSM/equivalent approved protected provider new grant/release signing blocked Email provider SMTP/relay notifications delayed only ERP optional integration optional integration reconciliation/commercial import delayed Telemetry store separate/optional separate/optional analytics delayed; licensing unaffected

docs.title: Network exposure principle
docs.text: Only required interfaces are exposed. Edge local APIs remain local by default. Customer-hosted network/port matrix must be generated by deployment packaging before production release.

docs.title: Upgrade principle
docs.text: Central LMS upgrade and edge product OTA are separate lifecycles. Customer-hosted LMS upgrades are manual package operations initially; edge application/model updates remain managed through LMS release/deployment functions.

docs.title: Core Sequence Diagrams
docs.text: This page defines implementation-level interaction expectations between the central LMS and edge/application components.

docs.title: First-time registration and base activation
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    actor A as Vendor Admin
    participant P as LMS Portal/API
    participant D as Device Agent
    participant R as Device Registry
    participant C as Capacity Service
    participant E as Entitlement Engine
    participant S as Signing Service
    participant L as Local License Agent
    A->>P: Create customer/site + enrollment authorization
    D->>P: Enrollment request + public key + fingerprint + inventory
    P->>R: Validate token, ownership, duplicates
    R-->>P: Registered device identity
    P->>C: Pre-assess base workload
    C-->>P: Advisory result
    P->>E: Check approved commercial entitlement
    E-->>P: Entitlement + limits
    P->>S: Sign device-bound base grant
    S-->>P: Signed grant
    P-->>D: Deliver grant
    D->>L: Import grant
    L->>L: Verify signature, binding, term, revision
    L->>L: Local capacity + health validation
    L-->>P: Activation receipt when connected

docs.title: Online trial activation
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    actor U as Customer Admin
    participant M as Marketplace
    participant P as Policy/Entitlement
    participant C as Capacity
    participant R as Release Service
    participant D as Device
    U->>M: Start trial
    M->>P: Validate eligibility (customer entitlement + feature)
    P-->>M: Eligible + configured duration
    M->>C: Pre-assess workload
    C-->>M: Recommendation/result
    M->>R: Resolve compatible release/model set
    M-->>D: Signed trial grant + required artifacts
    D->>D: Verify + local capacity + install + health-check
    D-->>M: First successful activation receipt
    M->>P: Start trial clock at activation time

docs.title: Offline / air-gapped trial activation
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant D as Device
    participant O as Relay/Media
    participant L as LMS
    participant S as Signing/Artifacts
    D->>O: Export signed trial request + nonce + inventory
    O->>L: Transfer request
    L->>L: Validate trial eligibility + capacity pre-assessment
    L->>S: Create signed trial grant + minimal compatible bundle
    S-->>L: Response package
    L-->>O: Approved response
    O-->>D: Controlled-media import
    D->>D: Verify request binding, grant, artifacts, local capacity
    D->>D: Install + health-check + activate
    D-->>O: Signed activation receipt
    O-->>L: Reconcile receipt; start trial clock from successful activation

docs.title: Feature purchase and add-on activation
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    actor U as Customer/Admin
    participant M as Marketplace
    participant E as ERP/Commercial
    participant L as LMS Entitlement/Policy
    participant R as Release Service
    participant D as Device
    U->>M: Request purchase
    M->>E: Commercial approval/payment workflow
    E-->>L: Approved commercial state
    L->>L: Create/update entitlement item + allocation
    L->>L: Issue superseding/add-on grant
    L->>R: Resolve compatible package/model set
    R-->>L: Release set
    L-->>D: Grant + release set
    D->>D: Verify dependencies + local capacity + health
    D-->>L: Accepted/active receipt

docs.title: Capacity reassessment after hardware/workload change
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant D as Device
    participant C as Central Capacity
    participant L as Local Capacity
    participant A as Admin
    D->>C: New inventory/resource/workload snapshot
    C->>C: Recalculate using benchmark profile
    C-->>A: Pass/warning/fail + recommendations
    A->>D: Choose approved configuration if adjustment needed
    D->>L: Reassess actual local combined workload
    L-->>D: Authoritative activation decision
    Note over D,L: Commercial entitlement is unchanged

docs.title: Online software/model update
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant L as LMS Deployment
    participant D as Update Manager
    participant R as Runtime
    L-->>D: Deployment target + signed release-set manifest
    D->>D: Preflight license/compatibility/disk/capacity
    D->>L: Fetch only missing artifacts/models
    D->>D: Verify signatures/hashes
    D->>D: Preserve known-good release set
    D->>D: Stage + migrate
    D->>R: Restart/start target services
    R-->>D: Health result
    alt Health OK
      D->>D: Commit target release set
      D-->>L: Installation receipt
    else Health failed
      D->>D: Roll back coherent previous release set
      D-->>L: Failure/rollback receipt
    end

docs.title: Offline software/model update
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant D as Device
    participant O as Relay/Media
    participant L as LMS
    D->>O: Export request + installed release/model inventory
    O->>L: Import request
    L->>L: Resolve minimal delta bundle
    L-->>O: Signed release set + only missing artifacts
    O-->>D: Import package
    D->>D: Verify + preflight + stage + migrate + health-check
    alt Success
      D->>D: Commit
    else Failure
      D->>D: Rollback
    end
    D-->>O: Signed installation receipt
    O-->>L: Reconcile

docs.title: Renewal for offline device
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    actor U as Customer
    participant L as LMS
    participant S as Signing Service
    participant O as Offline Relay
    participant D as Device
    U->>L: Renewal request / commercial approval
    L->>S: Sign superseding grant revision
    S-->>L: Signed renewed grant
    L-->>O: Export response package
    O-->>D: Controlled-media transfer
    D->>D: Verify revision, binding, term, supersession
    D-->>O: Signed acceptance receipt
    O-->>L: Reconcile receipt

docs.title: Device replacement / rehost
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    actor A as Authorized Admin
    participant O as Old Device
    participant N as New/Changed Device
    participant L as LMS
    A->>L: Submit replacement/rehost request
    N->>L: Register new cryptographic identity/fingerprint
    L->>L: Validate ownership + approval + allocation
    L->>L: Retire/suspend old binding
    L->>L: Reassign/return allocation
    L-->>N: New device-bound superseding grant
    N->>N: Verify and activate
    N-->>L: Acceptance receipt

docs.title: Device transfer
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    actor A as Requester
    actor B as Approver
    participant L as LMS
    participant D as Device
    A->>L: Request customer/site transfer
    L->>L: Validate current rights and target ownership
    L-->>B: Maker-checker approval request
    B->>L: Approve
    L->>L: Supersede invalid old grants + update ownership/site assignments
    L-->>D: New valid grant/policy state
    D-->>L: Acceptance receipt

docs.title: Revocation
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    actor A as Admin
    participant L as LMS
    participant D as Connected Device
    participant O as Air-gapped Device
    A->>L: Revoke grant/device
    L->>L: Record revocation + superseding state
    L-->>D: Deliver at sync/check-in
    D->>D: Enforce revoke
    Note over O,L: Air-gapped enforcement waits for signed import or offline expiry

docs.title: Failed update and rollback
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant L as LMS
    participant D as Update Manager
    participant R as Runtime
    L-->>D: Target release set
    D->>D: Verify + stage + install
    D->>R: Health check
    R-->>D: FAIL
    D->>D: Restore previous app/plugin/UI/model/config set
    D->>R: Verify rollback health
    alt Rollback healthy
      D-->>L: Rolled-back receipt
    else Rollback failed
      D-->>L: Critical failure receipt / escalate
    end

docs.title: Check-in freshness expiry
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant D as Device
    participant L as License Agent
    D->>L: Runtime authorization check
    L->>L: Compare last successful authorized check-in to policy
    alt Fresh
      L-->>D: Continue
    else Stale but grace/revalidation policy allows restricted state
      L-->>D: Restricted/grace + recovery path
    else Authorization no longer valid
      L-->>D: Disable unauthorized analytics; preserve recovery/diagnostics where allowed
    end

docs.title: Commercial expiry and grace
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant R as Runtime
    participant L as License Agent
    R->>L: Feature authorization request
    L->>L: Evaluate commercial valid_until independently from offline freshness
    alt Commercial term active
      L-->>R: Allow subject to other gates
    else Expired and grace active
      L-->>R: Grace/restricted behavior per policy
    else Expired and grace ended
      L-->>R: Deny analytics execution; keep recovery/diagnostics where allowed
    end

docs.title: State Machines
docs.text: State transitions are explicit, auditable and transactional where business integrity requires it.

docs.title: Device
docs.text:
PENDING -> REGISTERED -> ACTIVE -> SUSPENDED -> RETIRED
                         |
                         +-> REHOST_REQUIRED

docs.title: Grant / License
docs.text:
DRAFT -> ISSUED -> DELIVERED -> ACCEPTED -> ACTIVE -> GRACE -> EXPIRED
                                               |
                                               +-> REVOKED

ISSUED does not mean the device has received it. DELIVERED does not mean the device accepted it.

docs.title: Trial
docs.text:
ELIGIBLE -> REQUESTED -> ISSUED -> ACTIVE -> EXPIRED
                                      |
                                      +-> CONVERTED

Trial time begins when activation succeeds, not when the request or grant is issued.

docs.title: Purchase Request
docs.text:
REQUESTED -> REVIEW -> APPROVED -> PAID/COMMERCIAL_CONFIRMED -> GRANT_ISSUED
                  |
                  +-> REJECTED

A purchase request or catalog entry never authorizes execution by itself.

docs.title: Offline Request / Response
docs.text:
CREATED -> EXPORTED -> RECEIVED -> APPROVED -> RESPONSE_ISSUED -> IMPORTED -> RECONCILED
                           |            |
                           |            +-> REJECTED
                           +-> EXPIRED

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
AVAILABLE -> DOWNLOADED/IMPORTED -> VERIFIED -> STAGED -> INSTALLING -> HEALTH_CHECK -> ACTIVE
                                                              |             |
                                                              |             +-> ROLLED_BACK
                                                              +-> FAILED

docs.title: Renewal
docs.text:
DUE_SOON -> REQUESTED -> APPROVED_GRANT_ISSUED -> DELIVERED_IMPORTED -> ACCEPTED_ACTIVE
                |                   |                     |
                +-> REJECTED       +-> FAILED            +-> FAILED
                                                            |
                                                            +-> EXPIRED_RESTRICTED

docs.title: Governance rule
docs.text: Any implementation-specific state must map cleanly to these business states or be documented as an internal sub-state. UI/API must not collapse distinct business milestones that affect support or audit.

docs.title: System Context & External Boundaries
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    VA[Vendor Admin / Support / Release] --> LMS[LMS Control Plane]
    CA[Customer / Site Admin] --> LMS
    ERP[ERP / Billing] <--> LMS
    IDP[Future OIDC / SSO IdP] --> LMS
    SMTP[Email / Notification Provider] <--> LMS
    STORE[(Artifact Repository)] <--> LMS
    KMS[Protected Signing / KMS-HSM] <--> LMS
    LMS <--> EDGE[Edge Devices / Servers]
    RELAY[Authorized Offline Relay] <--> LMS
    RELAY <--> EDGE
    LMS --> OBS[Monitoring / Logs / Audit Export]

docs.title: Ownership boundaries
docs.text:
• LMS owns operational entitlement, grant, deployment, capacity and lifecycle state.
  • ERP owns financial/order truth when integrated.
  • Signing provider owns protected private-key operations.
  • Artifact repository stores immutable release/model binaries, not commercial truth.
  • Edge owns final local license verification, actual runtime capacity validation and installation commit/rollback.
  • Relay transports signed packages and has no issuance authority.

docs.title: Trust boundaries
docs.text: Human portal sessions, device cryptographic identity, signing infrastructure, artifact storage and offline media are separate trust zones. Data crossing each boundary is authenticated, authorized and validated according to the relevant security section.

docs.title: Failure-domain principle
docs.text: Loss of a non-critical external dependency should not silently corrupt licensing state. Email failure must not undo a renewal; telemetry failure must not invalidate a license; artifact-store failure must not mutate entitlement; signing failure queues/retries issuance rather than producing unsigned grants.

docs.title: System Design Requirements (SDR)
docs.text: This section is the normative, testable design-requirement baseline for LMS. It converts the architecture and business rules into uniquely identified requirements that engineering, QA, security and operations can trace to implementation and acceptance evidence.

docs.title: Requirement language
docs.text:
• SHALL = mandatory requirement.
  • SHOULD = expected unless an approved exception exists.
  • MAY = optional capability.
  • Every SHALL requirement must be traceable to implementation and verification evidence before production release.

docs.title: 19. Open decisions that constrain SDR implementation
docs.text:
The following are deliberately not frozen by this SDR yet: production OIDC/SSO provider/profile; exact model content-key wrapping and edge secure storage; final edge release archive format; product/hardware-specific benchmark thresholds; telemetry privacy/residency/retention policy; enterprise HA topology/RTO/RPO; final generated OpenAPI/physical DDL; historical-version support window.

Implementation SHALL preserve the documented abstraction until the owning decision is approved.

docs.title: 20. Requirement traceability template
docs.text:
Use this structure in implementation planning:

SDR ID          : SDR-LIC-003
Design / ADR    : Entitlements & Allocations / relevant ADR
Implementation  : issue/epic/PR
Test            : automated test ID / test report
Release evidence: build/release link
Owner           : module/team
Status          : planned | implemented | verified | accepted

An SDR requirement is not considered verified merely because code exists; evidence must demonstrate the stated behavior.

docs.title: Trust Boundaries
docs.text: The LMS has multiple trust zones. Security decisions must be based on which boundary data crosses, not only whether a request is 'internal'.

docs.title: Trust zones
docs.text: Zone Trusted for Not trusted for Human browser/session authenticated user intent after authn/authz tenant/object authority without server checks LMS application business policy/orchestration production signing private-key custody PostgreSQL transactional state signing authority or executable artifact trust Artifact repository immutable artifact storage deciding entitlement or execution rights Signing service/KMS/HSM protected cryptographic operations commercial policy decisions Edge device local enforcement/actual runtime evidence central commercial truth Offline relay/media transport only signing, entitlement or device authority ERP commercial/order truth where integrated device grant/runtime truth

docs.title: Central boundary
docs.text: Commercial authorization is evaluated centrally. The application sends an authorized signing request to the protected signing boundary; it never loads raw production signing private keys.

docs.title: Edge boundary
docs.text: The edge verifies signature, key trust, subject binding, commercial term, revision/supersession, dependencies, offline freshness/grace, package/model integrity, compatibility and local capacity before execution.

docs.title: Offline boundary
docs.text:
Offline request/response packages must be safe even if the relay/media is untrusted.

sequenceDiagram
    participant D as Device
    participant R as Relay / Media
    participant L as LMS
    participant S as Signing Service
    D->>D: Generate request_id + nonce + signed request
    D->>R: Export request
    R->>L: Transport only
    L->>L: Validate tenant/device/policy/replay
    L->>S: Authorized signing request
    S-->>L: Signed grant/manifest
    L-->>R: Device-bound response package
    R-->>D: Controlled-media transfer
    D->>D: Verify signature/hash/request binding/revision
    D->>D: Local capacity + install/health
    D-->>R: Signed receipt

docs.title: Boundary rules
docs.text:
• every cross-zone input is authenticated/validated according to its trust source
  • object IDs are not authorization
  • artifact location is not proof of integrity
  • relay possession is not proof of device authorization
  • database possession is not signing authority
  • local device reports are evidence and may be stale/tampered on a compromised host
  • telemetry failure does not alter commercial entitlement
  • email/notification failure does not roll back business transactions

docs.title: Failure containment
docs.text: External dependency failures use transactional outbox/retry rather than corrupting commercial state. Signing outage blocks new signed issuance but does not invalidate already valid grants. Artifact outage blocks delivery, not entitlement. ERP outage delays reconciliation, not local device enforcement.

docs.title: Grant issuance
docs.text: POST /v1/grants/issue is privileged/internal. It consumes an approved entitlement/allocation/policy snapshot and must be idempotent. Direct client-supplied limits are not trusted without policy validation.

docs.title: Offline exchange
docs.text: POST /v1/offline/requests/import validates request ID, nonce, device signature, device ownership and request age before any grant/package generation.

docs.title: Installation receipt
docs.text: POST /v1/installations/receipts records package/model versions, hashes, health result, rollback status and accepted grant revision.

docs.title: Protocol and versioning
docs.text:
• HTTPS outside local development
  • REST/JSON baseline with /v1 major version prefix
  • explicit content type and UTF-8
  • UTC ISO-8601 timestamps
  • opaque IDs; clients do not parse identifier structure
  • breaking semantic changes require new major API version or migration contract

docs.title: Authentication principals
docs.text: Human API calls use the configured human identity/session mechanism. Device APIs use registered device cryptographic identity or an explicitly documented enrollment bootstrap flow. Internal workers use dedicated least-privilege service identities.

docs.title: Authorization
docs.text: Every protected endpoint evaluates permission plus customer/product/site/device/object scope. Client-supplied tenant identifiers never grant access.

docs.title: Common headers
docs.text:
Authorization: Bearer <token>       # human/service where applicable
X-Request-ID: <uuid>
Idempotency-Key: <opaque-uuid>      # retry-safe write workflows

Device-signed endpoints may additionally carry key ID/signature/nonce fields in their canonical request envelope.

docs.title: Request rules
docs.text:
• schema validation at boundary
  • maximum payload/upload sizes
  • unknown critical fields rejected where signed canonicalization requires strictness
  • pagination/filter limits on collections
  • optimistic revision supplied for concurrent mutable resources where needed

docs.title: Response rules
docs.text: Successful responses use a consistent data + meta envelope. Errors use the stable error model. Security-sensitive failures may intentionally generalize external messages.

docs.title: Idempotency
docs.text: Required for grant issuance, activation, offline import, payment/commercial callbacks, deployment creation and other retried write workflows. Same key + different request hash is rejected.

docs.title: Pagination
docs.text: Cursor pagination is preferred for large/ordered collections. APIs define stable sort order, maximum page size and tenant-scoped filters.

docs.title: Long-running operations
docs.text: Release builds, large deployments, offline bundle generation and other long operations return a job/resource identifier rather than holding an HTTP request open. Job state is durable and observable.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Additive optional fields are allowed within /v1. Removal, type changes, changed meaning, newly required fields or changed security semantics require explicit compatibility handling.

docs.title: Endpoint catalogue
docs.text: The authoritative inventory is maintained in API Endpoint Catalogue; generated OpenAPI becomes the executable contract once implementation begins.

docs.title: Approval & Maker-Checker Workflows
docs.text: Everyday operations should remain efficient; high-risk overrides require independent approval.

docs.title: Single-actor operations
docs.text: Examples: allocating quantity within an already approved entitlement, normal renewal after approved commercial status, publishing a QA release, standard device registration.

docs.title: Maker-checker operations
docs.text: Require separate requester and approver for: - creating/increasing commercial entitlement outside imported/approved order state - perpetual or exceptional custom grant - trial extension beyond campaign/customer policy - forced rehost after major identity change - override of security/capacity block - Stable/LTS production promotion - emergency revocation override - signing-key rotation/activation administrative workflow

docs.title: State model
docs.text:
DRAFT -> SUBMITTED -> APPROVED -> EXECUTED
              |           |
              +-> REJECTED+-> CANCELLED

Approval records capture requester, approver, reason, policy evaluated, object revision, timestamps and execution result.

docs.title: Audit Event Catalogue
docs.text: Audit events are append-only and designed for investigation, compliance evidence and operational traceability.

docs.title: Retention
docs.text: Baseline retention is configurable 1–3 years. Customer/regulatory requirements may extend it. Deletion/retention jobs must themselves be audited.

docs.title: Background Jobs & Scheduler
docs.text: Background execution is a first-class backend subsystem with durable, idempotent jobs.

docs.title: Job families
docs.text:
• renewal reminders
  • trial expiry processing
  • stale offline-check-in detection
  • grace/restriction transitions
  • grant delivery/reconciliation retries
  • notification delivery
  • ERP reconciliation
  • deployment orchestration and rollout scheduling
  • artifact retention/cleanup
  • telemetry aggregation/export
  • audit retention/export
  • capacity reassessment requests triggered by reported changes

docs.title: Reliability rules
docs.text:
• Jobs are idempotent.
  • Durable job state survives application restart.
  • Retryable failures use bounded exponential backoff.
  • Non-retryable validation/security failures enter failed/dead-letter state.
  • A job records customer/tenant scope explicitly.
  • Duplicate execution must not issue duplicate grants or double-apply entitlement changes.
  • Jobs that cause external side effects use the transactional outbox pattern where appropriate.

docs.title: Scheduling
docs.text: Time-based jobs use UTC internally. Customer/site timezone is applied for maintenance windows and user-facing schedules.

docs.title: Observability
docs.text: Expose queue depth, oldest-pending age, success/failure/retry rate and dead-letter count per job family.

docs.title: Operational ownership
docs.text: Support/operations can retry or cancel only approved job classes. Privileged reprocessing that can alter commercial/license state is audited and may require approval.

docs.title: Mandatory database controls
docs.text:
• All business tables carry customer/tenant ownership directly or through an enforceable FK path.
  • Allocation updates and grant supersession occur in a single business transaction where possible.
  • Idempotency keys have unique constraints at the workflow boundary.
  • Mutable business objects carry revision/version columns for optimistic concurrency.
  • Audit events are append-only.
  • UTC is used for persisted timestamps; site timezone is display/scheduling context only.

docs.title: Error Model
docs.text: Errors must be machine-readable, stable and safe to expose. Internal stack traces are never returned to clients.

docs.title: Envelope
docs.text:
{
  "error": {
    "code": "LMS-GRANT-409-001",
    "message": "Grant revision is older than the active device revision.",
    "category": "conflict",
    "retryable": false,
    "details": {"active_revision": 8, "submitted_revision": 7}
  },
  "meta": {"request_id": "req_..."}
}

docs.title: Categories
docs.text: Category Typical HTTP Examples validation 400/422 malformed scope, invalid quantity authentication 401 invalid user/device credential authorization 403 cross-tenant access, unapproved override not_found 404 device/release does not exist in caller scope conflict 409 duplicate allocation, stale revision, rehost required rate_limit 429 enrollment or request abuse protection dependency 424 required base grant/model/runtime unavailable temporary 503 signing gateway/artifact service unavailable

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Error codes are documented and never repurposed.
  • retryable reflects workflow semantics, not only HTTP class.
  • Security-sensitive reasons may be intentionally generalized externally while full detail is written to audit/secure logs.
  • Offline import errors must be deterministic enough for field operators to recover without site debugging.

docs.title: Database Indexing, Transactions & Concurrency
docs.text: Tier-1 reliability depends on explicit concurrency behaviour, not only schema shape.

docs.title: Transaction boundaries
docs.text:
Use one database transaction for operations where partial success would violate commercial truth, including: - entitlement-pool reallocation across multiple devices - grant revision + supersession record creation - renewal term update + grant issuance record preparation - device decommission + allocation return - approval execution state transitions

External calls such as signing and artifact storage should use an outbox/saga-style pattern when they cannot participate in the DB transaction.

docs.title: Optimistic concurrency
docs.text: Mutable aggregates carry revision or version. Update commands include expected revision. A mismatch returns a conflict rather than overwriting concurrent changes.

docs.title: Initial index strategy
docs.text:
• unique(customer_id, external_reference) where integration keys apply
  • unique(device_id, active key status constraint)
  • index(customer_id, status) on customer-scoped collections
  • index(device_id, collected_at desc) for inventory/snapshots
  • unique(entitlement_id, feature_id, active pool identity) as model permits
  • index(grants: device_id, status, valid_until)
  • unique(grant_id, revision)
  • index(capacity_assessments: device_id, assessed_at desc)
  • unique(feature_id, version) and unique(model_id, version)
  • index(deployment_targets: job_id, status)
  • index(audit_events: customer_id, occurred_at desc) and object lookup indexes

Exact indexes must be validated against production-like query plans before launch.

docs.title: Idempotency storage
docs.text: Persist key, operation, request hash, response reference, created_at and expiry. Same key + different request hash is rejected.

docs.title: Database Migration Policy
docs.text: Database evolution must be safe across SaaS and customer-hosted deployments.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Alembic is the only supported schema migration path.
  • Production schema changes are reviewed like application code.
  • Destructive migrations are never combined with the first release that stops using the old field/table.
  • Prefer expand-and-contract for risky changes.
  • Migrations must be idempotent at deployment orchestration level and never require manual SQL at customer sites.

docs.title: Expand-and-contract example
docs.text:
Release N: add new nullable column/table + dual-read/write where needed
Release N+1: backfill/verify + switch reads
Release N+2: stop writing old field
Release N+3: remove old field after support window

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text: Before Stable promotion, verify whether application rollback is compatible with the migrated schema. If schema rollback is unsafe, the release must use backward-compatible migration design rather than assuming DB downgrade.

docs.title: Customer-hosted
docs.text: Each release package declares supported source schema versions and target schema version. Update Manager blocks unsupported upgrade jumps and provides a clear required intermediate version.

docs.title: Backend Modules — Detailed Responsibilities
docs.text: This page defines the initial modular-monolith boundaries. Modules may share one deployable process and database while maintaining explicit ownership and service interfaces.

docs.title: Identity & Access
docs.text:
Responsibilities: - development username/password authentication - session/token issuance - role and permission evaluation - tenant/customer scope enforcement - future OIDC/SSO adapter boundary

Must not: - own commercial entitlement logic - directly mutate device grants

docs.title: Customer, Site & Topology
docs.text:
Responsibilities: - customer lifecycle - site lifecycle and timezone - device ownership relationships - device-to-site assignments including multi-site server topology - transfer/decommission coordination

Key invariants: - a device has one commercial owner at a time - site assignments are explicit and auditable - transfer never silently overwrites previous ownership

docs.title: Device Enrollment
docs.text:
Responsibilities: - enrollment authorization creation - single-use/short-lived enrollment token validation - public-key registration - fingerprint version validation - duplicate/prior-registration detection - initial hardware inventory capture

Outputs a registered device identity only; registration does not grant paid rights.

docs.title: Catalog
docs.text: Responsibilities: - products - features - dependencies - compatibility metadata - marketplace visibility - release/model associations

docs.title: Entitlements
docs.text:
Responsibilities: - commercial rights - subscription/perpetual term - entitlement pools - update-right policy - ERP synchronization boundary

Entitlements are customer-owned business truth and are not directly executable on a device.

docs.title: Allocation
docs.text:
Responsibilities: - distribute pooled quantities to device/site scopes - validate total quantity - support reallocation - create a stable snapshot used for grant generation

Reallocation affecting multiple devices must be transactionally coordinated.

docs.title: Policy Engine
docs.text:
Responsibilities: - trial duration - offline validity - grace - update rights - co-termination - release-channel eligibility - override hierarchy - maker-checker requirement determination

Resolution hierarchy is explicit and deterministic: platform -> product -> customer/entitlement -> site/device exception where supported.

docs.title: Grant Service
docs.text:
Responsibilities: - construct canonical device-bound grant payload - resolve dependencies and constraints - revision and supersession - signing request - issuance record - delivery/reconciliation state

Signing private-key operations are delegated to the signing boundary.

docs.title: Capacity Service
docs.text:
Responsibilities: - inventory normalization - benchmark lookup - current+proposed workload calculation - feasibility result - recommended alternatives - assessment evidence/versioning

Must never mutate commercial entitlement automatically.

docs.title: Marketplace
docs.text: Responsibilities: - feature discoverability - customer/device eligibility - trial/purchase initiation - capacity preview - current entitlement and release readiness view

docs.title: Release & Artifact Management
docs.text: Responsibilities: - feature/application/UI/runtime releases - release channels - signed manifest metadata - artifact repository references - compatibility/dependency graph - release-set composition

docs.title: Model Management
docs.text: Responsibilities: - model identity/version - encryption metadata - compatibility - model-only OTA - device model inventory reconciliation

docs.title: Deployment Orchestration
docs.text: Responsibilities: - target selection - automatic/manual policy - maintenance-window scheduling - concurrency - per-device state - retry policy - rollback observation - installation receipt reconciliation

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text: Responsibilities: - renewal reminders - commercial renewal workflow - offline check-in freshness - grace/restriction - revocation - rehost - decommission

docs.title: Audit & Notification
docs.text: Audit is append-only for privileged and business-significant events. Notification starts with portal + email and retains an adapter boundary for webhooks.

docs.title: Observability & Initial SLO Baseline
docs.text: SLOs below are proposed engineering targets and must be finalized with business/operations before production launch.

docs.title: Golden signals
docs.text:
• availability
  • latency
  • error rate
  • saturation
  • queue/backlog depth
  • external dependency health

docs.title: Proposed service indicators
docs.text: Capability Indicator Initial target Core LMS API successful non-maintenance requests 99.9% monthly SaaS Read API latency p95 < 500 ms excluding artifact transfer Write API latency p95 < 1 s excluding signing/package build Signing request p95 < 2 s under normal load Audit persistence successful append 99.99% Deployment orchestration state not lost across restart 100% durable

docs.title: Required telemetry
docs.text:
• structured JSON logs with request/correlation ID
  • metrics per endpoint/module/error code
  • distributed trace context at central service boundaries
  • signing gateway latency/failure metrics
  • artifact storage latency/error metrics
  • deployment success/rollback rates
  • renewal/check-in backlog

No secrets, private keys, raw passwords or decrypted model material may appear in logs.

docs.title: API compatibility rule
docs.text: Within /v1, additive fields are allowed, removal/semantic repurposing is not. Breaking changes require a new API version or a documented migration window.

docs.title: Transactional Outbox & Internal Events
docs.text: External side effects must not cause commercial/database state to become inconsistent when a network dependency fails.

docs.title: Pattern

docs.title: Capacity Management
docs.text: Capacity management answers what this hardware can run at the target performance, independently from what the customer commercially owns.

docs.title: Four independent states
docs.text:
A feature/device combination must keep these states separate:

  1. Licensed — commercial right exists.
  2. Compatible — OS/runtime/hardware/dependency requirements are satisfied.
  3. Capacity Validated — combined workload meets the performance target or an approved warning policy.
  4. Installed / Healthy — required application/model components are installed and healthy.

A feature activates only when all required gates pass.

docs.title: Authority model
docs.text:
Central Capacity Engine performs advisory pre-assessment using reported inventory, workload definitions and approved benchmark profiles.

Local Capacity Engine performs the authoritative activation check using current drivers, resources, active streams, installed versions and actual local runtime conditions.

docs.title: Core process
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A[Collect stable inventory] --> B[Check compatibility]
    B --> C[Describe current + proposed workloads]
    C --> D[Select approved benchmark profiles]
    D --> E[Calculate combined resource budget]
    E --> F[Compare against target/headroom policy]
    F --> G{PASS / WARNING / FAIL}
    G -->|PASS| H[Recommend activation]
    G -->|WARNING| I[Recommend constrained configuration]
    G -->|FAIL| J[Recommend alternatives / hardware change]
    H --> K[Local authoritative recheck]
    I --> K
    J --> K
    K --> L[Monitor runtime and reassess on change]

docs.title: Non-negotiable rules
docs.text:
• Capacity never silently reduces purchased entitlement.
  • Licensed camera/feature quantity is not itself a capacity calculation.
  • Existing and proposed workloads are evaluated together.
  • Central advice may become stale; local activation remains authoritative.
  • Capacity recommendations are explicit and operator-selectable.
  • Benchmark evidence is versioned and governed.
  • Runtime changes can invalidate an old assessment.

docs.title: Authority split
docs.text:
Central Capacity Engine performs advisory pre-assessment using reported inventory and benchmark profiles.

Local Capacity Engine is authoritative for actual activation because it sees current runtime, active streams, drivers, local resources and installed components.

docs.title: Activation gate
docs.text: A feature may activate only when: 1. grant is valid 2. compatibility constraints pass 3. required package/model is installed and healthy 4. local combined-workload capacity validation passes for the selected configuration

docs.title: Recommendation mode
docs.text:
The engine recommends; it does not silently reconfigure commercial use.

Example for licensed People Counting 8 + PPE 4 when full combined workload fails: - PC 8 + PPE 2 - PC 4 + PPE 4 - reduce FPS/resolution - select optimized model/runtime - move one workload to another device - upgrade hardware

The customer/admin explicitly chooses an allowed recommendation. Purchased entitlement remains People Counting 8 + PPE 4 unless a commercial change is separately made.

docs.title: Confidence and evidence
docs.text: Assessment records should include benchmark profile/version, inventory version, workload inputs, result, limiting resource, recommendations and confidence/evidence quality.

docs.title: Benchmark Profile Governance
docs.text: Benchmark data is production engineering evidence. It requires versioning, ownership and release discipline.

docs.title: Benchmark profile dimensions
docs.text: A profile may be keyed by: - hardware class/model - accelerator/GPU architecture and VRAM - driver/runtime stack - feature/model/version - resolution/FPS/codec - decode path - inference backend and precision - concurrent workloads - measured latency/FPS/utilization/headroom

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
DRAFT -> VALIDATING -> APPROVED -> ACTIVE -> SUPERSEDED -> RETIRED

Only APPROVED/ACTIVE benchmark profiles may drive production recommendations.

docs.title: Evidence requirements
docs.text: Each benchmark profile records: - benchmark version - test hardware identity/class - software/runtime versions - test dataset/workload definition - warm-up period - sample duration - measured throughput/latency - CPU/RAM/GPU/VRAM/decode utilization - temperature/throttling observations - target/headroom thresholds - test date and owner - approval status

docs.title: Matching
docs.text: The Capacity Engine chooses the closest valid profile using explicit compatibility rules. It must not silently use a materially different hardware/runtime profile without reducing confidence or marking the result unsupported.

docs.title: Confidence
docs.text: Suggested confidence categories: - high: exact or validated-equivalent profile - medium: approved near-match with bounded interpolation - low: weak match; recommendation only, activation may require local empirical validation - unsupported: no valid evidence

docs.title: Headroom
docs.text:
Capacity results should expose remaining headroom for limiting resources when measurable. Example: GPU compute headroom 14%, VRAM headroom 22%, CPU headroom 35%.

Thresholds are product/benchmark policy, not hard-coded globally.

docs.title: Default decision mode
docs.text: The Capacity Engine recommends a feasible configuration. The customer/admin explicitly selects the configuration. The platform must never silently lower camera count, FPS, resolution or purchased entitlement.

docs.title: PASS
docs.text: Activation may proceed if all licensing, compatibility, installation and health gates also pass.

docs.title: WARNING
docs.text: Activation may proceed only if product policy permits warning acceptance. The selected configuration and warning acknowledgement are audited.

docs.title: FAIL
docs.text: Normal activation is blocked. The system presents recommendations such as reduced active workload, lower FPS/resolution, alternative model/runtime, moving workloads, second device or hardware upgrade.

docs.title: Exceptional override
docs.text:
If the company chooses to support a capacity override for exceptional cases, it is a privileged maker-checker action and must: - never change the commercial entitlement - capture requester, approver, reason and expiry - bind to a specific device/workload/release/model context - be time-limited or revision-limited - generate an audit event - be visible in support/operations views - automatically become invalid when material hardware/runtime/workload state changes

A capacity override must not bypass hard technical incompatibility such as unsupported architecture, missing required runtime or invalid package/model signature.

docs.title: Recommendation selection
docs.text: The selected recommendation becomes part of the activation/deployment record so later support can distinguish licensed rights from the operator-selected active configuration.

docs.title: Inventory & Benchmarking
docs.text: Stable inventory and dynamic resource snapshots are stored separately.

docs.title: Stable inventory
docs.text:
Collect at minimum:

  • CPU model, architecture, physical/logical cores and relevant frequency/capability data
  • RAM total and configured limits
  • GPU model/architecture, VRAM and relevant compute capability
  • accelerators such as Jetson/NPU where applicable
  • storage total/free/filesystem/health evidence
  • OS distribution/version, kernel
  • GPU/accelerator drivers
  • CUDA, TensorRT, DeepStream and product runtime versions
  • camera workload descriptors: count, resolution, FPS, codec/decode requirements
  • installed services, application releases and model inventory

docs.title: Dynamic snapshots
docs.text:
Capture separately:

  • available RAM
  • free disk
  • GPU/accelerator utilization
  • temperature/throttling
  • active streams
  • active workloads
  • other runtime pressure signals needed by the local Capacity Engine

docs.title: Benchmark profiles
docs.text:
Capacity decisions use measured, versioned benchmark profiles across:

  • hardware class
  • analytics model/version
  • resolution
  • FPS
  • inference backend
  • decoder/pipeline
  • concurrent workloads
  • target latency/FPS/SLA

Instantaneous utilization alone is not a benchmark.

Every assessment must record the benchmark profile/version and inventory/workload inputs used so the result can be reproduced and audited.

docs.title: Combined Workload Planning
docs.text:
Capacity planning evaluates the complete active and proposed workload, not individual feature quotas in isolation.

flowchart TD
    A[Collect Inventory] --> B[Compatibility Check]
    B --> C[Load Existing Workloads]
    C --> D[Add Proposed Workload]
    D --> E[Resolve Approved Benchmark Profiles]
    E --> F[Calculate Combined CPU/RAM/GPU/VRAM/Decode/Disk/Thermal Budget]
    F --> G[Apply Performance + Headroom Targets]
    G --> H{PASS / WARNING / FAIL}
    H -->|PASS| I[Recommend Activation]
    H -->|WARNING| J[Recommend Approved Alternatives]
    H -->|FAIL| K[Block Normal Activation + Recommend Alternatives]
    I --> L[Local Authoritative Recheck]
    J --> L
    K --> L

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Commercial entitlement:

People Counting = 8 cameras
PPE = 4 cameras

The Capacity Engine does not assume 8 + 4 = 12 cameras is feasible. It evaluates the real combined workload using model/runtime/resolution/FPS/decode and concurrency evidence.

If the selected workload does not meet target performance, recommendations may include:

  • People Counting 8 + PPE 2
  • People Counting 4 + PPE 4
  • lower FPS
  • lower resolution
  • different decode path
  • optimized model/runtime
  • move a workload to another device
  • deploy a second device
  • hardware upgrade

The operator/customer chooses an allowed configuration. Purchased entitlement remains unchanged.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
A capacity assessment should return:

  • result: pass / warning / fail / stale
  • limiting resource(s)
  • compatibility blockers
  • benchmark profile/version
  • workload hash/input summary
  • expected/observed headroom
  • confidence/evidence quality
  • recommendations
  • assessment timestamp and freshness
  • whether local revalidation is required

docs.title: Reassessment & Runtime Monitoring
docs.text: Capacity is not a one-time registration result. Assessments become stale when relevant conditions change.

docs.title: Mandatory reassessment triggers
docs.text:
• hardware inventory change
  • GPU/accelerator or driver change
  • CUDA/TensorRT/DeepStream/runtime change
  • application/feature release change
  • model version change
  • camera count/resolution/FPS/codec change
  • new feature activation
  • feature deactivation that changes combined workload
  • site-to-device workload movement
  • benchmark profile superseded by a materially different approved profile
  • repeated runtime degradation or thermal throttling

docs.title: Runtime monitoring signals
docs.text: Where available, monitor: - achieved inference/processed FPS - p95/p99 inference latency - dropped/late frames - CPU/GPU utilization - VRAM/RAM pressure - decoder utilization - temperature/throttling - service health/restarts - active stream count

docs.title: Drift handling
docs.text:
Healthy -> Warning -> Reassess -> Recommendation / Operator Action
                     |
                     +-> Critical degradation -> protect service / fail feature according to runtime safety policy

Runtime degradation does not rewrite entitlement. It may trigger a new capacity assessment and recommendation.

docs.title: Assessment freshness
docs.text: Each assessment records inventory version, resource snapshot timestamp, workload hash, benchmark version and software/model versions. If any required input changes, the previous assessment becomes stale.

docs.title: Central vs local drift
docs.text: Central LMS may show an advisory result based on last reported evidence. The local Capacity Engine remains authoritative for activation because it can detect current real conditions.

docs.title: Telemetry integration
docs.text: Capacity history may be forwarded to telemetry/analytics for trend analysis, but transactional activation state stays in the operational LMS/device state model.

docs.title: Capacity Status Model
docs.text: Capacity-related states must remain separate from commercial licensing and installation state. UI, API and audit records must not collapse them into one boolean.

docs.title: Independent status dimensions
docs.text:
Dimension Meaning Example states Licensed Customer/device has valid commercial authorization not_entitled, entitled, grant_pending, grant_active Compatible Software/model can technically run on this platform/runtime unknown, compatible, incompatible, blocked_dependency Capacity validated Combined workload is expected to meet the defined performance target not_assessed, pass, warning, fail, stale Installed / healthy Required application/model components are present and healthy not_installed, staged, healthy, degraded, failed

These dimensions are evaluated independently and then combined for activation.

docs.title: Activation rule
docs.text:
Licensed
AND Compatible
AND Capacity Validated
AND Installed / Healthy
= Feature may activate

A commercial entitlement can be valid even when the device is incompatible or under-capacity. Capacity failure never removes purchased entitlement.

docs.title: Capacity result semantics
docs.text:
PASS — benchmark evidence and current local conditions meet target with required headroom.

WARNING — workload is likely feasible but headroom/confidence is below preferred target, or the operator must choose an allowed lower-load configuration.

FAIL — the selected combined workload does not meet the minimum activation target.

STALE — the assessment is no longer valid because inventory, runtime, model, workload or benchmark policy changed.

docs.title: Reason-code examples
docs.text:
CAP_GPU_VRAM_INSUFFICIENT
CAP_GPU_COMPUTE_BELOW_TARGET
CAP_CPU_HEADROOM_LOW
CAP_RAM_HEADROOM_LOW
CAP_DISK_FREE_LOW
CAP_RUNTIME_UNSUPPORTED
CAP_DRIVER_MISMATCH
CAP_DECODE_BUDGET_EXCEEDED
CAP_COMBINED_WORKLOAD_EXCEEDS_PROFILE
CAP_BENCHMARK_PROFILE_MISSING
CAP_INVENTORY_STALE
CAP_RESOURCE_SNAPSHOT_STALE

Reason codes are stable machine-readable values and map to operator-safe recommendations.

docs.title: Workload Model
docs.text: Capacity planning is based on actual workload characteristics rather than licensed quantity alone.

docs.title: Workload dimensions
docs.text: A workload profile should capture, where relevant: - feature/capability code - analytics model ID and version - camera/input count - per-input resolution - FPS - codec - decode path (CPU/GPU/hardware decoder) - inference backend - precision - batching/concurrency - preprocessing/postprocessing cost class - retention/output pipeline impact where applicable - site assignment - required performance target such as minimum processed FPS or maximum latency

docs.title: Example workload
docs.text:
{
  "feature_id": "ppe_detection",
  "model_id": "ppe_detector",
  "model_version": "7.3.0",
  "site_id": "site_a",
  "inputs": {
    "camera_count": 4,
    "resolution": "1920x1080",
    "fps": 10,
    "codec": "h264",
    "decode_path": "gpu"
  },
  "runtime": {
    "backend": "tensorrt",
    "precision": "fp16"
  },
  "target": {
    "min_processed_fps": 9.5,
    "max_p95_latency_ms": 250
  }
}

docs.title: Combined workload budget
docs.text:
The Capacity Engine evaluates all active workloads plus the proposed workload together.

Existing workload A
+ Existing workload B
+ Proposed workload C
----------------------
Combined CPU / RAM / GPU / VRAM / decode / storage / thermal budget

Licensed quotas must not simply be added and treated as capacity.

docs.title: Multi-site devices
docs.text: For a device serving multiple sites, the workload model retains site attribution but capacity is evaluated at the shared device resource level. Site limits constrain commercial use; shared hardware capacity constrains actual concurrent execution.

docs.title: Workload identity
docs.text: Persist a stable workload profile or canonical workload hash so assessments can be reproduced and compared over time.

docs.title: Open Decisions
docs.text:
Open decisions are intentional unresolved choices. They must have an owner, decision deadline/milestone and constraints so implementation does not accidentally choose by default.

Topic Status Must be decided before Constraints already fixed Production human authentication / OIDC / SSO / MFA profile Open production security freeze RBAC/scope independent of IdP; privileged MFA target Exact model key wrapping / secure local key storage Security ADR required production model OTA no universal password; protected KMS/HSM boundary; device/deployment authorization Telemetry privacy / opt-in / residency / retention Open production telemetry enablement licensing cannot depend on high-volume telemetry Final generated OpenAPI schemas/error catalogue freeze Open implementation/API freeze /v1, stable error codes, idempotency/scoping rules Enterprise HA topology and RTO/RPO Open enterprise SLA offering Phase 1 backup/recovery required Final release archive/package format Proposed ADR Update Manager implementation freeze signed manifest/artifacts, traditional package, Windows-compatible abstraction Benchmark thresholds/headroom per product/hardware Product/performance decision capacity production activation benchmark profiles versioned; local authority Supported historical-version upgrade window Release/Support decision first production upgrade policy manifest declares supported source versions

docs.title: Governance
docs.text: Each open decision is resolved through ADR/product/operations approval appropriate to its domain. Until resolved, implementation must preserve the documented abstraction instead of hard-coding a choice.

docs.title: Phase Exit Criteria
docs.text: Delivery phases are complete only when their defined outputs and evidence are accepted.

docs.title: Phase 1 — Trust foundation
docs.text: Exit: device identity, enrollment, signed grant canonicalization, verifier, anti-replay/rollback tests and signing-key separation demonstrated.

docs.title: Phase 2 — Registry & licensing
docs.text: Exit: customer/site/device topology, entitlement pools, allocations, grants, base/add-on rules, tenant authorization and audit tests pass.

docs.title: Phase 3 — Capacity
docs.text: Exit: inventory schema, workload model, benchmark governance, central assessment, local authoritative check, recommendations and reassessment triggers validated against representative hardware.

docs.title: Phase 4 — Marketplace & release management
docs.text: Exit: catalog, trial/purchase flow, release channels, signed manifests, artifact repository, dependency/compatibility checks and portal states complete.

docs.title: Phase 5 — Model OTA & deployment
docs.text: Exit: encrypted model delivery, model inventory, auto/manual deployment, maintenance windows, release-set health-check/rollback and model-only OTA proven.

docs.title: Phase 6 — Lifecycle/offline
docs.text: Exit: renewal, three clocks, check-in, grace, revocation, rehost, transfer, decommission, online/offline/air-gapped request-response and receipt reconciliation pass end-to-end tests.

docs.title: Phase 7 — Hardening
docs.text: Exit: VAPT disposition, performance/resilience testing, backup restore, DR exercise, operational runbooks, monitoring/alerting, support readiness, ERP reconciliation and production release approval complete.

docs.title: Ownership
docs.text: Each phase has named Product, Engineering, QA and Security/Operations approvers appropriate to the risk. Evidence is linked to issues/PRs/test reports/releases rather than accepted verbally.

docs.title: Implementation Phases
docs.text: Phases are dependency-ordered capability increments. A phase is not complete because code exists; it must satisfy the corresponding exit criteria and integration evidence.

docs.title: Phase 1 — Trust foundation
docs.text: Device identity/key storage, enrollment authorization, grant canonicalization/signing/verifier, trust-store/key-purpose separation and anti-replay/rollback foundations.

docs.title: Phase 2 — Registry & licensing
docs.text: Customer/site/device topology, RBAC/tenant scope, entitlement pools, allocations, base/add-on grants, audit and online base activation.

docs.title: Phase 3 — Hardware & capacity
docs.text: Stable inventory, dynamic snapshots, workload model, benchmark governance, central advisory assessment, local authoritative assessment and recommendations.

docs.title: Phase 4 — Marketplace & release management
docs.text: Product/feature catalog, trial/purchase request, artifact repository, release channels, signed release manifests, compatibility/dependency metadata and portal flows.

docs.title: Phase 5 — Model OTA & deployment
docs.text: Encrypted model lifecycle, model inventory, release sets, online deployment jobs, AUTO/MANUAL policy, maintenance windows, health-check, rollback and model-only OTA.

docs.title: Phase 6 — Lifecycle & offline
docs.text: Renewal, three clocks, check-in, grace/restriction, revocation, rehost/transfer/decommission, assisted-offline and fully air-gapped request/response/receipt flows.

docs.title: Phase 7 — Hardening & production readiness
docs.text: Production IAM decision, VAPT, supply-chain controls, key rotation/recovery exercise, performance/resilience tests, DR/restore exercise, monitoring/alerts, runbooks/support, ERP reconciliation and production approval.

docs.title: Dependency principle
docs.text: Do not defer edge integration/offline/security to the final phase. Each earlier phase includes the minimum edge, audit, authorization and test work needed to prove its vertical slice. Phase 7 hardens completed capabilities rather than discovering integration for the first time.
