docs.title: Edge / Application Engineering
docs.text:
The local product remains operational without continuous internet for its authorized offline period.

Core local components: Device Identity Agent, Hardware Inventory Agent, Local Capacity Engine, License Agent, Feature Update Manager and Analytics Runtime/Product Adapter.

docs.title: Identity material
docs.text:
• device-generated asymmetric key pair
  • centrally registered public key
  • versioned hardware fingerprint
  • MAC/network identifiers as supporting evidence only

docs.title: Fingerprint policy
docs.text:
Fingerprint comparison is weighted/tolerant rather than exact equality.

Minor changes normally trigger compatibility revalidation but do not require rehost: - RAM upgrade/replacement - storage replacement - NIC replacement - added accelerator where identity remains stable

Major changes enter REHOST_REQUIRED: - motherboard replacement - device private key loss/recreation - multiple core identity attributes change beyond tolerance

docs.title: Rehost flow
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Identity mismatch detected] --> B{Minor or Major?}
    B -->|Minor| C[Revalidate compatibility/capacity]
    C --> D[Continue with audit]
    B -->|Major| E[REHOST_REQUIRED]
    E --> F[Admin / maker-checker approval]
    F --> G[Register replacement identity]
    G --> H[Issue superseding device grant]
    H --> I[Return old allocation / retire old binding]

docs.title: License Agent
docs.text: The License Agent is the local policy-enforcement authority for licensed runtime features. It validates signed central authorization and exposes an explicit local authorization contract to analytics services.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• load and verify signed grants
  • validate trusted key ID/algorithm/canonicalization profile
  • enforce device/product/site binding
  • enforce commercial valid-from/valid-until
  • enforce offline freshness and grace independently
  • enforce revision/supersession/anti-rollback
  • resolve base/add-on dependencies
  • enforce quantity and dynamic constraints
  • use persisted last-known trusted time
  • expose effective feature state/reason codes
  • produce signed acceptance/check-in evidence where required

docs.title: Startup
docs.text: On service startup: 1. load protected local identity/trust state 2. validate persisted grant artifacts 3. reject rollback to a lower accepted revision 4. evaluate trusted-time state 5. publish effective authorization state 6. keep protected analytics disabled until authorization is established

docs.title: Authorization response
docs.text:
{
  "feature_id": "ppe_detection",
  "decision": "allow",
  "grant_id": "grant_1001",
  "revision": 8,
  "effective_limits": {"camera_count": 4},
  "commercial_valid_until": "2027-10-31T23:59:59Z",
  "offline_fresh_until": "2026-10-25T12:00:00Z",
  "reason_codes": []
}

Possible decisions are allow, restricted, and deny. Reasons are machine-readable and safe for support.

docs.title: Runtime enforcement
docs.text: Analytics services ask the License Agent at actual workload creation/change boundaries. A cached allow decision is bounded by grant/time/revision context and must be invalidated when grant/policy state changes.

docs.title: Failure behavior
docs.text: Invalid signature, wrong subject, revoked trust key, stale rollback revision or malformed signed payload fail closed. Central LMS unavailability alone does not immediately fail a still-valid offline grant.

docs.title: Recovery accessibility
docs.text: When license execution is denied, the device should retain access to license import, diagnostics, support status and recovery workflows where product safety allows.

docs.title: Local Component Interfaces
docs.text: Local components must interact through explicit contracts so product teams do not bypass licensing or update controls.

docs.title: License Agent API
docs.text:
Suggested local-only interface:

GET  /local/v1/license/status
POST /local/v1/license/import
POST /local/v1/license/check
GET  /local/v1/features/effective

license/check inputs feature, requested quantity/scope, product context and optional workload reference; output is allow/deny/restricted with reason code and effective grant revision.

docs.title: Capacity Engine API
docs.text:
POST /local/v1/capacity/assess
GET  /local/v1/capacity/latest

Inputs include current resource snapshot, existing workloads, proposed workloads and benchmark profile version. It returns pass/warning/fail plus recommendations; it never changes purchased rights.

docs.title: Update Manager API
docs.text:
POST /local/v1/releases/import
POST /local/v1/releases/install
POST /local/v1/releases/rollback
GET  /local/v1/releases/status
GET  /local/v1/models/inventory

Only the Update Manager may activate a release set. Product services must not unpack arbitrary marketplace files directly.

docs.title: Runtime adapter contract
docs.text: Analytics services must ask the License Agent for authorization at actual execution boundaries. UI state may mirror authorization but cannot be the enforcement layer.

docs.title: Local persistence
docs.text: Protected local state should include accepted grant revision/sequence, last-known trusted time, current release set, rollback release set, installed model inventory and latest signed receipt queue.

docs.title: Offline & Air-Gapped Workflows
docs.text: Offline support is a first-class product path, not an exception.

docs.title: Request package contains
docs.text:
• request_id and nonce
  • device identity/public-key reference
  • current grant revisions
  • installed release/model inventory
  • hardware inventory version and relevant workload
  • requested operation: activation, trial, renewal, release update, model update
  • device signature over canonical request payload

docs.title: Response package contains
docs.text:
• request_id/nonce binding
  • signed grant revision(s) where applicable
  • release-set manifest
  • only required/missing artifacts
  • encrypted model artifacts if required
  • signatures/hashes
  • expiry/import policy

docs.title: Local import order
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Read Package] --> B[Verify package signature/hash]
    B --> C[Verify request_id + nonce binding]
    C --> D[Verify device/product scope]
    D --> E[Reject replay / stale revision]
    E --> F[Resolve grant and dependencies]
    F --> G[Capacity re-check]
    G --> H[Stage release set]
    H --> I[Health check]
    I -->|Pass| J[Commit + activate]
    I -->|Fail| K[Rollback]
    J --> L[Generate signed receipt]

Revocation cannot be instantaneous on a fully air-gapped device; it becomes effective when new signed state is imported or when existing offline authorization expires.

docs.title: Release Set & Rollback Contract
docs.text: A deployment is defined as a coherent release set rather than an isolated application file.

docs.title: Example release set
docs.text:
release_set_id: rs_2026_10_18_01
application: 5.8.0
features:
  ppe: 4.2.1
ui: 2.5.0
runtime: 3.7.0
models:
  ppe_detector: 7.3.0
config_schema: 6

docs.title: Update transaction
docs.text:
1. Preflight compatibility, disk and policy checks.
  2. Preserve current known-good release set.
  3. Fetch/import only missing artifacts.
  4. Verify every artifact.
  5. Run automated config/database migrations.
  6. Start target services.
  7. Run warm-up and health probes.
  8. Atomically mark release set active.
  9. On failure restore previous release set and compatible config/model state.

Retention: compress and retain 2–3 known-good sets where storage permits; immediately previous known-good set is mandatory.

docs.title: Runtime Enforcement & Protected Local State
docs.text: License enforcement must occur at the actual service/runtime boundary, not only in portal/UI controls.

docs.title: Authorization decision
docs.text: Before starting or expanding a protected feature, the runtime adapter checks: 1. signed grant validity 2. device/product/site scope 3. grant revision/supersession 4. commercial term 5. offline freshness/grace 6. feature dependencies 7. requested quantity/limits 8. installed release/model compatibility 9. local capacity result 10. runtime health

docs.title: Fail-closed vs recoverability
docs.text: Unauthorized analytics execution fails closed. Recovery functions such as license import, diagnostics and support status should remain accessible where product safety permits.

docs.title: Protected local state
docs.text:
Persist at minimum: - device private-key reference/protected key handle - highest accepted grant revision/sequence - last-known trusted time - current grant set - current and previous known-good release set - installed model inventory - pending signed receipts - latest local capacity assessment/workload hash

State that prevents rollback/replay should use the strongest practical local protection available for the platform.

docs.title: Clock handling
docs.text: A suspicious backward clock jump does not automatically extend rights. The License Agent uses persisted trusted-time evidence and moves to revalidation/restricted behavior according to policy.

docs.title: Runtime quantity enforcement
docs.text: Camera/feature limits are checked when workloads are created/changed, not only at startup. A device serving multiple sites enforces both total device limits and applicable site constraints.

docs.title: Service restart
docs.text: After restart, the runtime reconstructs effective authorization from verified persisted grants and protected monotonic state before enabling protected analytics.

docs.title: Update Manager
docs.text: The Update Manager is the only component allowed to commit application/feature/UI/runtime/model release sets on the edge.

docs.title: Transaction
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Receive Deployment / Import Bundle] --> B[Validate Manifest Schema + Signature]
    B --> C[Validate Every Artifact Hash / Signature]
    C --> D[Check OS / Architecture / Runtime Compatibility]
    D --> E[Check License / Update Right]
    E --> F[Check Disk / Dependencies]
    F --> G[Local Capacity Preflight]
    G --> H[Preserve Known-Good Release Set]
    H --> I[Stage to Non-Active Location]
    I --> J[Run Signed Migration / Install Handlers]
    J --> K[Start / Restart Services]
    K --> L[Warm-up + Health Checks]
    L -->|Pass| M[Atomic Commit]
    L -->|Fail| N[Rollback Coherent Release Set]
    M --> O[Signed Installation Receipt]
    N --> O

docs.title: Preflight
docs.text: Validate manifest version, target product/device, OS/architecture, source-version support, config schema, required runtime/model versions, disk space, grant/update rights, maintenance policy and local capacity.

docs.title: Staging and execution
docs.text:
• never execute directly from download/import media
  • stage to dedicated path
  • installation/migration handlers are signed artifacts referenced by manifest
  • preserve previous known-good configuration/model set
  • apply least required privilege
  • make interrupted/restarted execution idempotent/recoverable

docs.title: Health checks
docs.text: Health checks include process/service status plus product-specific readiness/warm-up. Merely starting a process is not a successful deployment.

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text: Rollback restores application, plugins/features, UI/runtime, model versions and compatible configuration as one coherent release set. If rollback itself fails, emit critical failure receipt and require support/incident escalation.

docs.title: Download/import optimization
docs.text: Compare installed artifact/model inventory and fetch/import only missing required content. Existing artifact content is reused only after hash/version validation.

docs.title: Receipt
docs.text: Receipt records device, target release set, previous release set, grant revision, artifact/model versions, result, health outcome, rollback outcome and timestamps.

docs.title: Developer Setup
docs.text: This page defines the baseline local development workflow for the LMS handbook and the future application repositories.

docs.title: Required tools
docs.text:
• Python 3.12
  • Git
  • PostgreSQL client/server for backend development
  • Node.js LTS for React/Vite portal development
  • MkDocs dependencies from requirements.txt for handbook work

docs.title: Handbook preview
docs.text:
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate  # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
mkdocs serve

docs.title: Development principles
docs.text:
• Use synthetic data only.
  • Never use production signing keys in development.
  • Keep configuration outside source code.
  • Run migrations through Alembic only.
  • Use feature flags/policy configuration rather than ad-hoc code branches for customer exceptions.
  • Keep edge interfaces backward-compatible across supported release windows.

docs.title: Before opening a PR
docs.text:
• run unit/integration tests for affected code
  • run mkdocs build --strict for documentation changes
  • update ADRs when architecture changed
  • verify no secrets/customer data are included
  • document rollback/migration impact

docs.title: Recommended application repository shape
docs.text:
lms/
├── backend/
│   ├── app/
│   ├── migrations/
│   └── tests/
├── portal/
│   ├── src/
│   └── tests/
├── edge/
│   ├── identity/
│   ├── license_agent/
│   ├── capacity/
│   ├── update_manager/

└── .github/workflows/

The handbook may remain in this repository or a dedicated docs repository, but code ownership and documentation links must remain traceable.

docs.title: Standard local services
docs.text:
• PostgreSQL
  • artifact-storage emulator or local approved filesystem abstraction
  • development signing provider using non-production keys
  • backend API
  • portal dev server
  • optional local edge simulator/test agent

docs.title: Standard commands
docs.text:
Projects should expose consistent commands through Makefile/task runner/scripts, for example:

make setup
make lint
make test
make test-integration
make migrate
make run-backend
make run-portal
make docs
make security-scan

Exact tooling may differ, but CI and developer commands should invoke the same underlying checks.

docs.title: Seed data
docs.text: Development seed data should include synthetic customers, sites, devices, entitlements, grants, capacity profiles, marketplace features and release/model metadata so critical flows can be exercised locally without production data.

docs.title: Engineering Change Control
docs.text: Tier-1 governance requires traceability from business decision to code and production release.

docs.title: Change classes
docs.text: Class Example Required controls Standard bug fix, docs, non-risk refactor PR + tests + review Architecture new module, trust boundary, schema model ADR + architecture review + PR Security-sensitive signing, auth, import parser, model protection security review + tests + VAPT scope review Commercial-policy entitlement, expiry, trial, renewal rules product/commercial approval + regression tests Emergency critical security/production issue expedited approval + complete post-change review

docs.title: Traceability
docs.text: Every material production change should be traceable to requirement/issue, design/ADR where relevant, pull request, CI evidence, release identifier and deployment/audit event.

docs.title: Classes
docs.text: Class Examples Handling baseline Public approved public product docs may be shared externally Internal architecture, roadmaps, operational metrics company/internal access Confidential customer/device inventories, entitlement details, audit exports restricted need-to-know Highly Restricted signing private keys, credentials, model content keys, incident secrets dedicated protected systems; never normal docs/logs

docs.title: Repository rule
docs.text: This private handbook may contain Internal and selected Confidential design information, but never secrets, credentials, private keys, decrypted proprietary models or raw sensitive incident/customer exports.

docs.title: Logging rule
docs.text: Logs should contain identifiers and references, not full sensitive payloads unless explicitly approved for a secure diagnostic channel.

docs.title: Export rule
docs.text: Audit/report exports must enforce caller scope and may require additional approval depending on customer data sensitivity.

docs.title: Engineering Decision Gates
docs.text: Large work items pass explicit decision gates before production.

docs.title: Gate 0 — Problem/Sponsor
docs.text: Business outcome, owner, scope and success criteria approved.

docs.title: Gate 1 — Architecture Ready
docs.text: Trust boundaries, state model, data ownership, APIs and ADR impact reviewed.

docs.title: Gate 2 — Development Ready
docs.text: Stories, acceptance criteria, dependencies, test approach and environment needs are ready.

docs.title: Gate 3 — Release Candidate
docs.text: Code complete, migrations/upgrades/rollback tested, security scans complete, docs current.

docs.title: Gate 4 — Production Approval
docs.text: QA evidence, release notes, known issues, VAPT/security disposition, rollout/rollback plan and approvals complete.

docs.title: Gate 5 — Post-Release
docs.text:
Deployment health, incidents, customer feedback, metrics and follow-up actions reviewed.

Gate evidence should be traceable to issues/PRs/releases rather than captured only in meetings.

docs.title: Branching model
docs.text:
Use short-lived branches from main. main must remain releasable/documentation-buildable. Long-lived feature branches are discouraged.

Suggested naming:

feature/<ticket>-short-name
fix/<ticket>-short-name
security/<ticket>-short-name
docs/<ticket>-short-name

docs.title: Pull request requirements
docs.text: Every PR contains: - problem/business context - implementation summary - affected modules - API/schema/migration impact - security impact - test evidence - rollback/compatibility notes where applicable - documentation/ADR updates

docs.title: Review rules
docs.text: At least one qualified reviewer for normal changes. Sensitive areas require an additional domain reviewer: - authentication/RBAC/signing/offline parser -> Security - entitlement/grant/policy -> Backend architecture/product owner - release/update/model OTA -> Release/Edge owner - DB migration -> Backend/data owner

docs.title: Merge policy
docs.text: Prefer squash or rebase according to repository setting, but final history must retain ticket/PR traceability. Direct commits to protected main should be disabled once team development begins.

docs.title: Commit content policy
docs.text: No secrets, private keys, customer exports, production credentials, decrypted model artifacts or proprietary binary releases should be committed to the documentation/source repository.

docs.title: Handbook Status & Ownership
docs.text: This handbook is the normative internal engineering baseline for LMS unless a newer approved ADR or product decision supersedes a section.

docs.text:

  • Proposed — recommended design awaiting approval.
  • Open Decision — implementation must preserve flexibility until resolved.
  • Deprecated — retained for historical reference only.
  • Phase 2 — deliberately deferred capability.

docs.text: Normal allocations within an approved entitlement may be single-admin or automated. Sensitive actions such as entitlement increase, large custom/perpetual grants, trial extension, forced LTS, major rehost, security/capacity override and signing-key changes use maker-checker approval.

docs.title: Release Approval SOP
docs.text: This SOP governs promotion into production-capable channels.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
• Developer: produces Development/QA artifacts
  • QA: validates functional/integration/regression evidence
  • Security: validates security gates for applicable changes
  • Release Manager: owns promotion and rollout
  • Product/Architecture: approves material compatibility/policy impact when needed

docs.title: Promotion path
docs.text: Development -> QA -> Internal/Beta -> Stable -> LTS (explicit)

docs.title: Stable promotion evidence
docs.text: The promotion record references: - source commit/tag - build identity - signed release manifest - automated test report - upgrade/migration test - rollback test - compatibility matrix - capacity/benchmark impact if relevant - security scan/VAPT disposition - release notes - known issues and rollback trigger

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Stable promotion uses maker-checker: Release Manager requests; required QA/Security approver confirms evidence. Same actor must not self-approve when policy requires separation.

docs.title: LTS
docs.text: LTS is never automatic. Company explicitly designates an eligible Stable release as LTS after stability evidence and support-life decision.

docs.title: Emergency release
docs.text: Emergency releases may use an expedited path but still require source traceability, approval, signed artifacts, rollback plan and post-release review within the defined incident process.

docs.title: Section-by-Section Content Audit
docs.text: This audit is based on reading the actual handbook content, not counting files or headings. A section is marked Complete only when its core business rules, implementation contract, security/error behavior, tests and operations are materially documented or explicitly linked.

docs.title: Corrections from the earlier audit
docs.text: The earlier audit overstated completion in several areas. In particular, Security, Backend, Edge, QA, Operations, Telemetry and Architecture had pages whose titles existed but whose content was too thin. This audit intentionally distinguishes Complete baseline, Substantial, and unresolved implementation/open-decision work instead of equating a file's existence with coverage.

docs.title: What is intentionally not declared complete
docs.text:
1. production OIDC/SSO/MFA provider/profile
  2. exact model encryption key hierarchy/wrapping/local secure storage
  3. final release archive/package execution format
  4. product-specific benchmark/headroom thresholds and hardware matrix
  5. telemetry privacy/residency/retention commercial policy
  6. enterprise HA topology and contractual RTO/RPO
  7. generated OpenAPI and final physical DDL/index tuning
  8. final UI visual/accessibility design system
  9. product/version support lifetime policy

These are explicit decisions or implementation artifacts; they must not be hidden by calling the handbook 'fully complete'.

docs.title: Engineering
docs.text:
• Typed Python where practical.
  • Pydantic at API boundaries.
  • Alembic only for production schema changes.
  • Structured logs with correlation IDs.
  • Explicit domain/service boundaries.
  • Authorization tests for tenant-scoped data.
  • Idempotency for retried workflows.
  • No secrets in source control.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• Behaviour-changing PRs update the handbook.
  • Approved/proposed/open-decision status is explicit.
  • Mermaid is preferred for maintainable diagrams.
  • Material architecture changes require ADRs.
  • Real customer data is never used in examples.

docs.title: ERP Integration Contract
docs.text: ERP and LMS remain separate systems. Integration is intentionally narrow so the LMS does not become an accounting platform.

  "event_type": "order_line_approved",
  "occurred_at": "2026-10-18T10:00:00Z",
  "customer_external_ref": "CUST-1007",
  "contract_ref": "CTR-2031",
  "order_ref": "SO-9001",
  "line": {
    "product_code": "ANALYTICS_BASE",
    "feature_code": "PPE",
    "quantity": 40,
    "term": {"type": "subscription", "start": "2026-11-01", "end": "2027-10-31"}
  }
}

docs.title: Integration rules
docs.text:
• ERP events are idempotent by event_id.
  • Unknown product/SKU mapping is quarantined for review.
  • Payment/renewal status alone does not directly modify a device grant; LMS first updates entitlement state and then issues a new grant revision.
  • ERP retries are safe.
  • LMS never overwrites financial truth back into ERP unless a separate outbound contract explicitly permits it.

docs.title: Reconciliation
docs.text: A scheduled reconciliation compares approved ERP commercial lines against LMS entitlements. Differences are categorized as missing, extra, quantity mismatch, term mismatch or mapping failure and surfaced to operations without destructive auto-correction.

docs.title: Licensing Overview
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    E[Customer Entitlement Pool] --> A[Allocation]
    A --> G[Device-bound Signed Grant]
    G --> V[Local Verification]
    V --> R[Runtime Permission]

This separates commercial ownership from device execution.

docs.title: Transfer between customer/site ownership contexts
docs.text:
1. Create transfer request with current owner/site, requested owner/site, reason and effective intent.
  2. Validate caller authority and affected entitlements/allocations.
  3. Require approval according to policy; cross-customer transfer is always sensitive.
  4. Freeze or supersede grants that would become invalid under the new ownership.
  5. Update ownership/site assignments only after approval.
  6. Issue new grants under the valid target entitlement context.
  7. Reconcile old allocations and audit before/after ownership.

Silent overwrite of owner/site is prohibited.

docs.title: Replacement device
docs.text: For device replacement: - register replacement identity as a new device - approve replacement/rehost relationship - return or reassign allocation from retired device - issue new device-bound grant - retire old device/grant binding - preserve audit lineage between old and replacement devices

docs.title: Rehost
docs.text: Rehost is used when the physical system is intended to remain the same commercial installation but cryptographic/major hardware identity changed. Major motherboard/key changes enter REHOST_REQUIRED until approved.

docs.title: Revocation
docs.text:
Connected device: central revocation/superseding state is delivered at next sync/check-in according to policy.

Air-gapped device: immediate remote revocation is impossible. Revocation becomes effective after importing signed updated state or when current offline authorization expires.

docs.title: Diagnostics in grace/restricted state
docs.text: Where product safety permits, grace/restricted mode should preserve access to diagnostics, license recovery/import, support status and existing customer data. Expired commercial rights should disable unauthorized analytics execution, not make recovery impossible.

docs.title: Entitlements & Allocations
docs.text:
Example entitlement: PPE = 40 camera rights.

Device A = 16
Device B = 12
Device C = 8
Unallocated = 4

The customer/admin may redistribute rights without a new purchase while total allocation stays within the purchased pool.

docs.title: Reallocation controls
docs.text:
1. Validate total allocation.
  2. Calculate affected device grants.
  3. Issue superseding revisions.
  4. Prevent temporary double-allocation beyond approved transition policy.
  5. Synchronize online or through offline package.
  6. Audit before/after values and actor.

docs.title: Customer, device and site scope
docs.text:
A device is commercially owned by one customer but may serve multiple sites through explicit device-site assignments.

A device-bound grant may contain site-specific limits. Example:

{
  "device_id": "dev_x",
  "capability": "ppe_detection",
  "site_limits": [
    {"site_id": "site_a", "max_cameras": 4},
    {"site_id": "site_b", "max_cameras": 8}
  ]
}

The grant remains bound to the device, while constraints may partition the permitted quantity by site.

docs.title: Allocation invariant
docs.text:
For every entitlement item:

sum(active allocations) <= purchased/approved entitlement quantity

Reallocation must preserve this invariant transactionally and must not rely on UI-only validation.

docs.title: Signed Grant Canonical Format
docs.text: The signed grant is a device-verifiable authorization artifact. The final binary/serialization format is implementation-specific, but signing semantics must be deterministic.

docs.title: Canonical payload example
docs.text:
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "grant_id": "grant_001",
  "revision": 8,
  "supersedes": "grant_000",
  "issued_at": "2026-10-18T12:00:00Z",
  "subject": {
    "customer_id": "cust_001",
    "product_id": "analytics",
    "device_id": "dev_001"
  },
  "capabilities": [
    {
      "code": "ppe_detection",
      "limits": [{"key": "camera_count", "op": "lte", "value": 4}],
      "dependencies": [{"capability": "analytics_base", "required": true}]
    }
  ],
  "commercial": {"type": "subscription", "valid_until": "2027-10-31T23:59:59Z"},
  "runtime": {"offline_days": 7, "grace_days": 7},
  "key_id": "lic_sign_01"
}

docs.title: Signing requirements
docs.text:
1. Remove the signature field from the payload.
  2. Normalize field order/encoding using a documented canonicalization method.
  3. Hash/sign the canonical bytes using the active license-signing key.
  4. Attach key_id, algorithm and signature.
  5. Device reconstructs the same canonical bytes before verification.

docs.title: Anti-rollback
docs.text: Device persists the highest accepted revision/sequence per relevant grant lineage and rejects older revisions unless an explicit signed recovery mechanism exists.

docs.title: Key rotation
docs.text: Verification trust store may contain current and retiring public keys. New grants use only the active key; older valid grants remain verifiable during the planned rotation window.

docs.title: Device-Bound Grants
docs.text:
A grant is the signed executable permission derived from entitlement, allocation and policy.

{
  "grant_id": "grant_1001",
  "device_id": "dev_310",
  "capabilities": [{
    "feature": "ppe_detection",
    "limit": {"type": "camera_count", "value": 4}
  }],
  "runtime_policy": {"offline_days": 7, "grace_days": 7},
  "revision": 2,
  "supersedes_grant_id": "grant_0988",
  "signature": "..."
}

Supersession is mandatory for replacement grants to prevent accidental aggregation.

Perpetual licenses may carry explicit update policies such as unlimited, N future major updates, or until-version.

docs.title: Dynamic License Policy Model
docs.text: The license system must avoid feature-specific columns such as ppe_enabled. Rights are represented by generic grants, constraints and dependencies.

docs.title: Grant model
docs.text: A grant contains: - subject scope: customer/product/device/site - capability code - grant type: base/add-on/trial/perpetual/subscription - quantity/limit constraints - valid-from / valid-until - offline/grace policy - revision and supersession - dependencies - update-right policy - signature metadata

docs.title: Constraint examples
docs.text:
[
  {"key": "camera_count", "op": "lte", "value": 8},
  {"key": "site_id", "op": "in", "value": ["site_a", "site_b"]},
  {"key": "model_family", "op": "in", "value": ["ppe_v7"]}
]

docs.title: Update-right policy
docs.text:
Preferred explicit schema:

{
  "mode": "remaining_major_updates",
  "remaining_updates": 1,
  "until_version": null
}

Supported modes may include unlimited, during_active_term, remaining_major_updates, until_version, and none.

docs.title: Dependency semantics
docs.text: Dependent add-ons become dormant when required base grants are not active unless explicitly marked independent by policy.

docs.title: Renewal & Offline Validity
docs.text:
Three clocks remain independent:

  1. Commercial term/expiry.
  2. Offline authorization freshness — default 7 days unless overridden by policy.
  3. Grace/restriction period — default 7 days unless separately overridden.

A successful check-in never extends the paid commercial term.

A payment or central entitlement renewal does not activate an offline device until the new signed grant revision is delivered/imported and accepted locally.

docs.title: Reminder baseline
docs.text:
Default proposed reminders are 30 days, 7 days and 1 day before expiry, configurable by product/customer policy.

flowchart LR
    A[Due Soon / Reminder] --> B[Renewal Requested]
    B --> C[Commercial Approval]
    C --> D[Entitlement Term Updated]
    D --> E[New Signed Grant Revision]
    E --> F{Delivery}
    F -->|Online| G[Delivered]
    F -->|Offline| H[Export / Import]
    G --> I[Local Verify]
    H --> I
    I --> J[Atomic Accept / Active]
    J --> K[Receipt / Reconciliation]

docs.title: Status milestones
docs.text:
• Due Soon
  • Requested
  • Approved / Grant Issued
  • Delivered / Imported
  • Accepted / Active
  • Failed / Rejected
  • Expired / Restricted

Issued != Delivered != Accepted.

If delivery or verification fails, the old grant continues according to its own expiry/grace rules. Where product safety permits, restricted/grace mode should preserve diagnostics, license recovery/import and access to existing customer data while unauthorized analytics execution is disabled.

docs.title: Trials
docs.text:
• Default trial period is 7 days.
  • Duration is policy/campaign configurable by feature, product or approved customer exception.
  • Trial starts at first successful feature activation, not request, issuance, package download or import.
  • Trial is a signed time-limited device-bound grant, not a UI flag.
  • Baseline eligibility is one trial per customer entitlement + feature.
  • Admin/campaign override may permit extension or an additional trial, but the override is auditable and may require maker-checker approval.
  • Globally reusable trial licenses are prohibited.

docs.title: Add-ons
docs.text:
Subscription add-ons normally co-terminate with the active base subscription.

Base: Jan 1 ---------------- Dec 31
PPE:                 Sep 1 -- Dec 31
Renewal: Jan 1 ---- Base + PPE together

Commercial pricing may be prorated for the remaining base term. An explicitly independent add-on may carry its own term when product/commercial policy permits it.

Perpetual base licenses may have subscription add-ons.

Dependent add-ons become dormant when their required base is inactive unless the add-on policy explicitly marks them independent.

docs.title: Purchase/activation distinction
docs.text: A trial request, purchase request, payment approval or marketplace selection does not itself authorize runtime execution. The device still requires a valid signed grant and all compatibility/capacity/install/health gates.

docs.title: Marketplace & OTA
docs.text:
Marketplace and OTA are separate capabilities in one LMS.

  • Marketplace: what can this customer/device discover, trial or buy?
  • OTA: how are compatible application/model components safely delivered, installed and rolled back?

They reuse the same customer, device, entitlement, capacity and audit data.

docs.title: Deployment Job State Machine
docs.text: Deployment orchestration must be restart-safe and deterministic.

docs.title: Job states
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Draft
    Draft --> Scheduled
    Scheduled --> Running
    Running --> Completed
    Running --> PartiallyFailed
    Running --> Failed
    Scheduled --> Cancelled
    Running --> Cancelling
    Cancelling --> Cancelled

docs.title: Target states
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Pending
    Pending --> WaitingWindow
    WaitingWindow --> Preflight
    Preflight --> Downloading
    Downloading --> Verifying
    Verifying --> Staging
    Staging --> Installing
    Installing --> HealthCheck
    HealthCheck --> Active
    HealthCheck --> RollingBack
    RollingBack --> RolledBack
    Preflight --> Blocked
    Verifying --> Failed
    Installing --> Failed

docs.title: Retry policy
docs.text:
• Network/artifact transient failures may retry with exponential backoff.
  • Signature/hash/compatibility failures are non-retryable until input changes.
  • Installation failure triggers rollback before retry consideration.
  • Automatic mode obeys maintenance window and concurrency limits.
  • Manual mode requires explicit deployment approval/start.

docs.title: Completion semantics
docs.text: A job is Completed only when every target reaches Active or an explicitly accepted terminal exclusion state. PartiallyFailed preserves successful targets and clearly reports failed/rolled-back targets.

docs.title: Deployment & Rollback
docs.text: Deployment turns an approved release set into per-device installation actions with policy, maintenance-window, concurrency, health and rollback controls.

docs.title: Policy hierarchy
docs.text:
Platform Default -> Product -> Customer -> Site -> Device Override

Supported settings include AUTO/MANUAL, channel, maintenance window, model-only OTA, application OTA, concurrency, rollout batch size and auto-rollback.

Default automatic maintenance window: 01:00–03:00 in site timezone, customer configurable.

docs.title: Target resolution
docs.text: Before scheduling, LMS resolves target customer/site/device ownership, entitlement/update rights, device status, compatible release-set path and maintenance policy. A target that becomes ineligible before install is revalidated and blocked.

docs.title: Rollout strategies
docs.text:
• all-at-once only for explicitly accepted small/low-risk scope
  • batch/concurrency-limited rollout
  • canary/pilot subset before broader rollout where risk warrants
  • pause/stop on configured failure threshold
  • forced rollout requires privileged approval when policy marks it sensitive

docs.title: Per-target execution
docs.text:
Pending -> Waiting Window -> Preflight -> Download/Import -> Verify -> Stage -> Install -> Health Check -> Active
                                                              |
                                                              +-> Rollback -> Rolled Back

docs.title: Preflight gates
docs.text:
• release/channel eligibility
  • current/source version supported
  • grant/update right valid
  • OS/architecture/runtime compatible
  • dependencies/model versions resolvable
  • disk space and rollback reserve
  • local capacity check
  • package/trust-store compatibility

docs.title: Success semantics
docs.text: A target is successful only after health check and atomic commit. Downloaded or installed files alone do not mean Active.

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text: Rollback restores a coherent release set, not one binary. Keep 2–3 known-good releases when disk permits; the immediately previous known-good set is mandatory.

docs.title: Automatic stop criteria
docs.text: Systemic signature/hash failure, repeated migration failure, rollback failure, or failure-rate threshold should stop/pause further rollout and alert Release/Operations.

docs.title: Offline deployment
docs.text: Air-gapped deployment uses the same target/release semantics. The response bundle carries required release-set artifacts; final central state becomes authoritative only after signed installation receipt reconciliation.

docs.title: Model Manifest Schema
docs.text: Model metadata is independent from application releases so compatible model-only OTA does not force application redownload.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "manifest_version": 1,
  "model_release_id": "mr_ppe_7_3_0",
  "model_id": "ppe_detector",
  "version": "7.3.0",
  "channel": "stable",
  "framework": "TensorRT",
  "precision": "FP16",
  "input": {"width": 640, "height": 640},
  "compatibility": {
    "architectures": ["x86_64"],
    "gpu_families": ["nvidia"],
    "runtime": ">=3.7 <4.0",
    "feature_release": ">=4.2 <5.0"
  },
  "artifact": {
    "uri_ref": "artifact://models/ppe/7.3.0",
    "sha256": "...",
    "encrypted": true,
    "encryption_profile": "model-envelope-v1",
    "size": 901234567
  },
  "validation": {
    "warmup_required": true,
    "expected_output_schema": 3
  },
  "signature": {"key_id": "release_sign_01", "algorithm": "Ed25519", "value": "..."}
}

docs.title: Key handling principle
docs.text: The repository stores encrypted model material. Entitlement controls permission to use the model; device authorization controls decryption. A universal embedded model password is prohibited.

docs.title: Model OTA
docs.text: AI models are first-class managed artifacts with independent identity, versioning, compatibility, encryption, deployment and rollback.

docs.title: Model release metadata
docs.text: Each release records model ID/version, framework/backend, precision, input/output schema, feature compatibility, runtime range, accelerator/hardware compatibility, encrypted content hash, size, release channel and signing/encryption profile.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Create Model Release] --> B[Validate Metadata / Compatibility]
    B --> C[Encrypt Artifact with DEK]
    C --> D[Sign Manifest / Artifact]
    D --> E[Publish to Channel]
    E --> F[Resolve Authorized Target]
    F --> G[Compatibility + Capacity Check]
    G --> H[Download / Import Missing Content]
    H --> I[Verify Signature + Hash]
    I --> J[Authorize / Unwrap Content Key]
    J --> K[Stage Model]
    K --> L[Warm-up / Functional Health Check]
    L -->|Pass| M[Atomic Activate]
    L -->|Fail| N[Restore Previous Model]

docs.title: Independent OTA
docs.text: A compatible model-only release may deploy without application redownload. The manifest must declare compatible feature/runtime ranges, and local inventory prevents redundant download.

docs.title: Authorization and encryption
docs.text: Possessing the encrypted model file is not sufficient for use. The device needs both valid entitlement/grant authorization and authorized content-key unwrap/use according to the security model.

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text: Previous known-good model remains available when storage permits. If application/plugin and model versions are tightly coupled, they are deployed/rolled back as one Release Set.

docs.title: Inventory
docs.text: Edge reports model ID/version/hash/status. Central uses inventory for delta bundle generation and support visibility.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: Health/warm-up is model-specific and may include load success, inference sanity, expected output schema and latency/performance threshold. A hash-valid model that fails warm-up is not activated.

docs.title: Security boundary
docs.text: No universal model password is permitted. Exact key wrapping/local secure storage follows ADR-009.

docs.title: Release Manifest Schema
docs.text: The release manifest is the machine-readable contract between Release Management and the edge Update Manager. It is signed and immutable after publication.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "manifest_version": 1,
  "release_id": "rel_ppe_4_2_1",
  "feature_id": "ppe_detection",
  "version": "4.2.1",
  "channel": "stable",
  "platforms": [
    {"os": "ubuntu", "versions": ["22.04", "24.04"], "arch": ["x86_64", "aarch64"]}
  ],
  "requirements": {
    "runtime": ">=3.7 <4.0",
    "disk_free_mb": 2500,
    "ram_mb": 8192
  },
  "artifacts": [
    {
      "artifact_id": "art_app_421",
      "type": "application",
      "version": "4.2.1",
      "sha256": "...",
      "size": 123456789
    }
  ],
  "models": [
    {"model_id": "ppe_detector", "version_range": ">=7.3 <8.0", "required": true}
  ],
  "migrations": {
    "config_schema_from": [4,5],
    "config_schema_to": 6,
    "automatic": true
  },
  "health_checks": [
    {"type": "http", "target": "http://127.0.0.1:9000/health", "timeout_sec": 30}
  ],
  "rollback": {"supported": true, "minimum_free_mb": 3000},
  "signature": {"key_id": "release_sign_01", "algorithm": "Ed25519", "value": "..."}
}

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Manifest canonicalization is defined before signing.
  • Artifact hash is mandatory.
  • Dependencies use explicit version ranges.
  • Installation scripts are treated as signed artifacts, never unsigned inline commands.
  • A published manifest is immutable; corrections create a new release/version.
  • Device must reject unsupported manifest versions.

docs.title: Release Management
docs.text: Release Management governs creation, evidence, promotion, retirement and supportability of application, feature/plugin, UI/runtime and model-compatible releases.

docs.title: Channels
docs.text:
Development -> QA -> Internal/Beta -> Stable -> LTS -> Retired

Channel movement is a controlled promotion, not a file copy.

docs.title: Channel semantics
docs.text:
Channel Purpose Production eligible Development developer iteration No QA formal test candidate No Internal/Beta controlled non-general validation Restricted Stable default production release Yes LTS explicitly designated long-support release Yes Retired blocked from new deployment No

Automatic production updates consume Stable by default. LTS targeting is explicitly controlled by the company.

docs.title: Release evidence
docs.text: Before Stable promotion, the release record links to: - source commit/tag - CI/build identity - release manifest and artifact hashes - automated unit/integration/upgrade tests - migration result - rollback result - compatibility matrix - capacity/benchmark impact where relevant - security scan/VAPT disposition - SBOM/provenance record - release notes/known issues - rollout and rollback triggers

docs.title: Publication
docs.text: Published manifests/artifacts are immutable. Correction creates a new release/version. Artifact repository content alone does not make a release deployable; release state and approval govern eligibility.

docs.title: Traditional package standard
docs.text:
release/
├── manifest.json
├── application/
├── ui/
├── migrations/
├── configs/
├── dependencies/
├── install/
│   ├── install.sh
│   ├── rollback.sh
│   └── healthcheck.sh
└── signature

Install/migration/rollback handlers are signed artifacts. No normal production release depends on manual site migration.

docs.title: Retirement
docs.text: Retirement prevents new deployment. Existing installations are not silently removed. Support policy determines required upgrade path and emergency-block behavior.

docs.title: LTS
docs.text: LTS designation requires explicit support-life decision, supported upgrade paths, compatibility evidence and operational commitment. Stable does not automatically become LTS.

docs.title: Semantic versioning intent
docs.text: Application, feature/plugin and model versions should use a predictable version scheme. Semantic versioning is recommended for software interfaces where practical.

docs.title: Compatibility declarations
docs.text: Every release declares supported: - OS/version and architecture - application/runtime ranges - dependent feature/plugin ranges - model ranges - configuration schema versions - minimum hardware/runtime requirements

docs.title: Support window
docs.text: The organization must define how many previous application versions remain upgrade-supported. Until finalized, release manifests must explicitly declare supported source versions rather than assuming any historical version can upgrade directly.

docs.title: Breaking changes
docs.text: Breaking local API, manifest or grant-format changes require: 1. schema/version bump 2. compatibility/migration plan 3. dual-read or staged migration when necessary 4. explicit support-window communication 5. rollback testing

docs.title: Model compatibility
docs.text: Model releases are independently versioned but must declare compatible feature/runtime ranges. A model-only update is allowed only when those constraints pass.

docs.title: Backup & Recovery
docs.text: Backup/recovery protects business truth, deployment evidence and artifact availability without treating signing private keys as normal application data.

docs.title: Backup scope
docs.text:
• PostgreSQL transactional state
  • audit data
  • artifact metadata and release/model manifests
  • artifact repository binaries or replicated/versioned equivalent
  • deployment/configuration reconstruction metadata
  • operational configuration templates that do not contain raw secrets

Signing private keys use a separate KMS/HSM/provider recovery mechanism and are never copied into ordinary DB/file backups.

docs.title: SaaS Phase 1 baseline
docs.text:
• automated encrypted database backups
  • point-in-time recovery where chosen PostgreSQL platform supports it
  • object/artifact versioning or protected backup
  • backup job monitoring/alerting
  • documented restore procedure
  • regular restore exercise
  • single-primary acceptable initially while remaining HA-ready

docs.title: Customer-hosted baseline
docs.text: Installation package defines what the customer must back up, supported backup commands/provider integration, required artifact/config directories and restore ordering.

docs.title: Restore order
docs.text:
1. establish clean supported LMS environment
  2. restore PostgreSQL
  3. restore/attach artifact repository
  4. restore non-secret configuration/reconstruction metadata
  5. reconnect protected signing provider using its independent process
  6. run integrity/migration compatibility validation
  7. verify tenant/authz/audit state
  8. verify device check-in and safe signing integration

docs.title: Integrity checks
docs.text: Restore validation checks DB consistency, schema version, artifact hashes, manifest availability, audit continuity, application startup and tenant scoping.

docs.title: Recovery evidence
docs.text: Record backup identifier/time, recovery point, operator, restore duration, verification checks, exceptions and remediation.

docs.title: Open decision
docs.text: Exact contractual RPO/RTO remains an enterprise operations decision. Engineering must measure restore performance before any promise is made.

docs.title: Backup classes
docs.text:
• transactional PostgreSQL backups
  • artifact repository backups/replication
  • audit data backups
  • configuration/reconstruction metadata
  • signing-key recovery through its separate protected mechanism

docs.title: Proposed retention baseline
docs.text: Retention must be finalized by operations/compliance, but the implementation should support daily/weekly/monthly policy tiers and customer-specific extensions.

docs.title: Restore validation
docs.text: A backup is not considered reliable until restore is tested. Scheduled restore exercises verify: - DB integrity and migration compatibility - artifact hashes - audit availability - application startup - customer/tenant access behavior - signing integration restoration without exposing key material

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text: Restore exercises record backup ID, environment, restore duration, validation checks, failures/exceptions and remediation owner.

docs.title: Customer-Hosted Deployment Topology
docs.text: Customer-hosted LMS uses the same application codebase with deployment-mode configuration.

docs.title: Baseline topology
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    U[Customer/Vendor Admin Browser] --> RP[Reverse Proxy / TLS]
    RP --> LMS[LMS Application]
    LMS --> PG[(PostgreSQL)]
    LMS --> AR[(Artifact Repository / MinIO or approved storage)]
    LMS --> SG[Signing Gateway / configured secure provider]
    LMS --> SMTP[SMTP / notification relay]
    EDGE[Edge Devices] <--> LMS

docs.title: Minimum production requirements
docs.text:
• TLS termination
  • persistent PostgreSQL storage
  • persistent artifact storage
  • backup destination
  • secrets/configuration outside source code
  • monitoring/log export
  • time synchronization
  • outbound email if notifications are enabled

docs.title: Upgrade model
docs.text: Customer-hosted LMS self-update is manual in the initial product. Vendor supplies a signed LMS release package/runbook; customer/operator executes upgrade within an approved maintenance window.

docs.title: HA
docs.text: HA is an enterprise option rather than mandatory Phase 1 baseline. Exact topology and RTO/RPO are decided per deployment tier.

docs.title: Disaster Recovery & Continuity
docs.text: Phase 1 remains operationally simple but recovery is designed before production.

docs.title: Proposed recovery tiers
docs.text: Component Baseline approach PostgreSQL automated encrypted backups + tested restore Artifact repository versioned/replicated object storage or protected backup Audit data protected backup; append-only semantics Signing metadata database backup; private keys handled separately Signing keys KMS/HSM/provider-specific protected recovery Customer-hosted LMS documented manual restore package/process

docs.title: RTO/RPO
docs.text: Exact enterprise RTO/RPO remain an open business/operations decision. Until approved, no team should promise contractual recovery targets.

docs.title: Mandatory DR testing
docs.text:
• scheduled restore test
  • database migration + restore compatibility test
  • artifact integrity verification
  • signing-key recovery procedure exercise without exposing key material
  • documentation of measured restore time and exceptions

docs.title: Environment classes
docs.text: Environment Purpose Data rule Release channels Local Dev developer iteration synthetic only Development Integration service/edge integration synthetic/test Development/QA QA formal validation synthetic/anonymized QA/Internal Staging production-like readiness anonymized/approved Internal/Stable candidate Production customer service real customer data Stable/LTS only

docs.title: Separation requirements
docs.text:
• Separate credentials and secrets per environment.
  • Production signing keys are never available in lower environments.
  • Development/QA artifacts cannot be promoted implicitly into production; promotion creates explicit approved release state.
  • Test tenants/devices are clearly marked.
  • Production backups are not restored into lower environments without approved sanitization.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Configuration is supplied through environment/secret manager/deployment configuration, never hard-coded. Environment-specific settings include DB connection, artifact storage, signing provider, email provider, telemetry endpoints and auth mode.

docs.title: Time
docs.text: All servers use reliable time synchronization. Persist timestamps in UTC. Site timezone is used for display and maintenance-window interpretation.

docs.title: Incident Response
docs.text: Incident response covers security events and operational failures that materially affect licensing, tenant isolation, deployment, model protection or customer availability.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text: Detect -> Triage -> Classify -> Contain -> Preserve Evidence -> Recover -> Validate -> Communicate -> Post-Incident Review

docs.title: Immediate evidence
docs.text: Preserve: - request/correlation IDs - security/audit events - affected tenant/customer/device IDs - deployment job/target history - relevant application/security/edge logs - artifact/release hashes and manifest IDs - grant revisions - signing/trust key IDs (never raw private key material) - timestamps and operator actions - relevant approval records

docs.title: Containment rule
docs.text: Containment must avoid destroying evidence or making unsafe commercial changes. Do not bypass signature/tenant controls merely to restore service.

docs.title: Suspected signing-key compromise
docs.text:
1. stop new signing with affected key
  2. identify signed grants/releases and potential exposure window
  3. activate approved replacement key where available
  4. distribute trust-bundle update through supported routes
  5. assess air-gapped devices that cannot receive immediate trust changes
  6. supersede/revoke affected artifacts/grants where policy requires
  7. validate restored signing and initiate post-incident review

docs.title: Tenant-isolation incident
docs.text:
1. treat as security-critical until disproven
  2. restrict risky support/global access paths
  3. preserve request/query/audit evidence
  4. identify data read/write exposure and affected tenants
  5. remediate authorization/query defect
  6. add regression tests before reopening path
  7. follow legal/customer notification policy where applicable

docs.title: Artifact repository compromise / tampered release
docs.text:
1. stop affected deployments
  2. block suspect release/artifact identities
  3. verify signed manifest/content hashes from trusted build evidence
  4. rotate repository credentials if compromised
  5. rebuild/re-publish as a new release if needed
  6. inspect devices that received suspect content
  7. use rollback where active release is unsafe

docs.title: Model key / wrapping compromise
docs.text:
1. disable affected wrapping/master-key path
  2. identify model releases and wrapped-key scopes
  3. rotate KEK/wrapping configuration using approved provider process
  4. regenerate wrapped keys/release metadata as required
  5. assess offline devices unable to receive replacement authorization
  6. document IP/data exposure assessment

docs.title: Compromised human credential / privileged account
docs.text:
1. revoke sessions/tokens
  2. disable/reset identity through IdP/auth system
  3. review privileged actions/audit exports
  4. rotate any derived secrets exposed by the account
  5. restore access using approved identity recovery
  6. review role assignments and strengthen controls if needed

docs.title: Widespread bad release
docs.text:
1. stop/pause rollout
  2. mark release blocked
  3. rollback to known-good release set
  4. verify rollback health receipts
  5. preserve failed installation evidence
  6. communicate affected customers according to incident policy

docs.title: Malicious/malformed offline package exploit attempt
docs.text:
1. quarantine media/package
  2. preserve package hash and parser error evidence
  3. determine whether parsing occurred before signature verification
  4. block/revoke package/request identity as appropriate
  5. patch parser and add regression/fuzz case
  6. inspect similarly exposed devices

docs.title: Communications
docs.text: External communications contain confirmed impact, affected scope and recovery guidance only. Unvalidated technical hypotheses and sensitive security details remain internal until approved.

docs.title: Closure criteria
docs.text: Incident is closed only after containment, recovery validation, evidence retention, customer/internal communications, root-cause analysis, corrective actions with owners and regression/monitoring improvements are documented.

docs.title: SaaS deployment
docs.text:
1. Confirm release approval and backup/recovery readiness.
  2. Apply DB-compatible release using controlled deployment.
  3. Run migrations before/with application start according to migration contract.
  4. Verify API, DB, signing, artifact repository, notification and background-job health.
  5. Run smoke tests for login, device check-in, grant issuance in safe test scope and artifact access.
  6. Monitor errors/latency/queues after release.
  7. Roll back application when safe; do not blindly downgrade incompatible schema.

docs.title: Customer-hosted deployment
docs.text:
1. Validate supported source LMS version and environment prerequisites.
  2. Take verified backup of DB/artifact/config state.
  3. Verify signed vendor LMS package.
  4. Stop/coordinate services according to maintenance procedure.
  5. Execute automated application/migration package.
  6. Run health checks.
  7. Validate customer portal, device check-in and artifact/signing integration.
  8. Complete upgrade receipt/runbook record.

docs.title: Failure handling
docs.text: If migration/app startup fails, follow the release-specific recovery path. Never hand-edit production schema unless an approved emergency procedure explicitly requires it and captures the exact changes.

docs.title: Rollback decision
docs.text: Rollback feasibility is declared by the release. When DB migration is backward-compatible, application rollback may proceed. When not, use forward-fix/recovery procedure rather than unsafe schema downgrade.

docs.title: Post-deployment evidence
docs.text: Record release ID, operator, start/end time, source/target versions, migration result, health result, exceptions and rollback status.

docs.title: Monitoring & Operational Integration
docs.text: ERP contract details live in the Integrations section. This page defines operational monitoring responsibilities.

docs.title: Core health
docs.text: Monitor: - LMS API availability, latency and error rate - PostgreSQL connection/replication/storage health as applicable - background-job queue depth and oldest age - outbox pending/dead-letter count - signing-provider latency/failures - artifact repository latency/errors/capacity - authentication failure/rate-limit anomalies - notification delivery failures - backup success/age - deployment success/failure/rollback rate - device check-in freshness distribution - renewal/trial processing backlog - capacity assessment warning/fail/stale rate - ERP reconciliation mismatch/failure

docs.title: Alert classes
docs.text: Condition Example action API unavailable/high error Operations incident triage Signing unavailable Stop manual retries; queue issuance; escalate if customer impact Dead-letter growth inspect worker/dependency; replay only with approved procedure Backup stale/failed immediate operations investigation Rollback failure high-severity release incident Tenant/authz anomaly security escalation Check-in stale spike connectivity/systemic device investigation ERP mismatch spike integration/commercial reconciliation

docs.title: Dashboards
docs.text: Minimum production dashboards cover API/service health, DB/dependencies, signing, deployments, jobs/outbox, licensing lifecycle, capacity and backup status.

docs.title: Logging and correlation
docs.text: Central logs are structured and include request/correlation ID, tenant-safe object identifiers and stable error codes. Sensitive values remain redacted.

docs.title: ERP monitoring boundary
docs.text: ERP may be authoritative for orders/invoice/payment/contracts. LMS remains authoritative for operational entitlements, allocations, grants, activation, deployment and local acceptance. Integration failure is visible and reconciled; it does not silently rewrite either system.

docs.title: Notification Events & Templates
docs.text: Phase 1 channels are portal + email. The event model must allow webhooks later without changing business modules.

docs.title: Template rules
docs.text: Templates include customer/site/device display names, safe remediation steps and portal deep-link identifiers. They never include secrets, raw license payloads, private keys or decrypted model information.

docs.title: Delivery tracking
docs.text: Persist notification ID, event ID, recipient, channel, template version, send attempt, result and delivered timestamp. Repeated transient failures retry with backoff; permanent failures are visible to operations.

docs.title: Operational Runbook Baseline
docs.text: Runbooks must be executable by support/operations without requiring source-code knowledge.

docs.title: Required runbooks before production
docs.text:
1. LMS API unavailable
  2. PostgreSQL degraded/unavailable
  3. Signing service unavailable
  4. Artifact repository unavailable
  5. Failed Stable rollout
  6. Mass rollback
  7. Offline bundle rejected at customer site
  8. Device stuck in REHOST_REQUIRED
  9. Customer over-allocation conflict
  10. Suspected signing-key compromise
  11. Backup restore
  12. ERP synchronization mismatch

docs.title: Runbook format
docs.text: Each runbook contains: - symptoms and alerts - customer impact - safety checks - diagnostic steps - approved remediation - rollback/recovery - escalation owner - audit/evidence to retain - post-incident follow-up

docs.title: Incident severity proposal
docs.text: Severity Description Example Sev-1 broad critical outage/security compromise signing-key compromise, platform-wide license failure Sev-2 major customer/service impairment deployment/renewal failure affecting many devices Sev-3 limited degradation single-customer update issue with workaround Sev-4 minor/non-urgent cosmetic portal issue

docs.title: L1 — Operations / Support
docs.text: Handles known runbooks, customer/site/device lookup, entitlement/grant status checks, offline package validation and standard rehost/renewal coordination.

docs.title: L2 — Engineering
docs.text: Engaged for reproducible product defects, migration/update failures, capacity anomalies, integration issues and unsupported states not resolved by runbook.

docs.title: L3 — Architecture / Security / Release
docs.text: Engaged for signing/key incidents, tenant isolation, systemic release failures, data integrity risk, cross-module design defects and emergency architecture decisions.

docs.title: Escalation packet
docs.text:
Every escalation includes: - customer/site/device IDs - request/correlation ID - error code - timestamps/timezone - current grant/release/model revisions - deployment/installation receipt state - relevant safe logs - steps already attempted - business/customer impact

Avoid sending secrets or decrypted model material through ordinary support channels.

docs.title: Device cannot activate feature
docs.text:
1. Identify customer/site/device and request ID.
  2. Check registration state and device ownership.
  3. Check entitlement and allocation.
  4. Check latest grant issuance/delivery/acceptance state.
  5. Check commercial expiry, offline freshness and grace separately.
  6. Check device-reported rejection code.
  7. Check capacity/compatibility and installed release/model dependencies.
  8. If offline, validate request/response pairing and nonce.
  9. Apply only approved remediation; do not hand-edit grants.
  10. Record resolution/audit reference.

docs.title: Offline package rejected
docs.text:
1. Confirm package was created for the same device/request ID.
  2. Verify operator did not reuse an older response.
  3. Compare device accepted revision vs response revision.
  4. Check signature/key trust status.
  5. Check release/model compatibility.
  6. Export a fresh request if nonce/request expired or state changed.

docs.title: Deployment failed and rolled back
docs.text:
1. Confirm rollback health status.
  2. Capture installation receipt and request ID.
  3. Identify failed stage: download, verify, stage, migration, start, health check.
  4. Check disk/dependency/runtime prerequisites.
  5. Block release for broader rollout if systemic.
  6. Escalate to Release Manager when failure rate crosses rollout threshold.

docs.title: Rehost required
docs.text:
1. Confirm major hardware/key identity change.
  2. Verify customer/device ownership.
  3. Collect previous/new fingerprint evidence.
  4. Submit rehost request and required approval.
  5. Rebind identity and issue superseding grant.
  6. Retire old binding and return/reconcile allocation.

docs.title: Renewal approved but device still expired
docs.text:
1. Confirm ERP/commercial approval reached LMS.
  2. Confirm new entitlement term and grant revision exist.
  3. Check whether device has delivered/imported the new revision.
  4. For offline site, produce/import renewed response package.
  5. Confirm device accepted revision and generated receipt.

docs.title: Signing service unavailable
docs.text:
1. Stop repeated manual issuance attempts.
  2. Confirm signing gateway/provider health.
  3. Existing valid grants continue according to policy; do not bypass signature requirement.
  4. Queue issuance via outbox/retry.
  5. Escalate according to incident severity if customer activations/renewals are blocked.

docs.title: Customer/device Marketplace feature view
docs.text: Required fields: - feature name/code and description - screenshots or approved visual assets where available - release notes/current release - product/OS/runtime compatibility - capacity preview and recommendation - current entitlement/allocation state - trial eligibility and configured duration - purchase/request-purchase action and request status - dependency/model requirements - device installation/health status

docs.title: Admin catalog view
docs.text: Required fields/actions: - feature code/name/description - supported products/OS/architecture - minimum hardware/runtime requirements - dependencies - current release and channel - trial/commercial policy - campaign configuration - release status - model associations - marketplace visibility

docs.title: Device detail view
docs.text: Show separately: registration status, license/grant status, commercial expiry, offline freshness, grace state, capacity state, installed release set, model inventory, last check-in, site assignments and active deployment jobs.

docs.title: Renewal view
docs.text: Do not collapse lifecycle into a single 'renewed' flag. Display: Due Soon -> Requested -> Approved/Grant Issued -> Delivered/Imported -> Accepted/Active, plus Failed/Rejected and Expired/Restricted states.

docs.title: Audit UX
docs.text: Every sensitive action should expose actor, timestamp, object/revision, reason, approval status and resulting state without exposing secret material.

docs.title: Role-Based Portal UX
docs.text: The portal must present role-appropriate actions while backend authorization remains authoritative.

docs.title: Vendor Super Admin
docs.text: Views: global customers, products, incidents, signing/release health, privileged audit. Actions are tightly controlled and high-risk changes require approval.

docs.title: Product Admin
docs.text: Views/actions: product/feature catalog, entitlement policy, trial campaigns, commercial configuration and approved exceptions.

docs.title: Release Manager
docs.text: Views/actions: release candidates, QA/security evidence, channels, rollout plans, deployment status, rollback and LTS designation.

docs.title: Security Approver
docs.text: Views/actions: pending maker-checker requests, signing-key changes, rehost/security overrides, VAPT/security disposition.

docs.title: Customer Admin
docs.text: Views/actions: customer sites/devices, entitlement pool, allocations, trials, purchase requests, renewals, update policy, capacity recommendations.

docs.title: Site Admin
docs.text: Views/actions: site-scoped devices, workload/capacity state, maintenance window, deployment progress and permitted site allocations.

docs.title: Support Engineer
docs.text: Views/actions: diagnostic state, request IDs, grant delivery/acceptance, offline package state, rehost/renewal workflows and safe support actions. No hidden broad commercial override.

docs.title: Read Only / Auditor
docs.text: Views: status, reports and audit history without mutation.

docs.title: Critical UX rules
docs.text:
• Always distinguish registration, license, capacity and install/health status.
  • Always distinguish issued, delivered and accepted grants.
  • Show why an action is blocked with safe error/reason codes.
  • Offline export/import screens display request ID, target device, expiry, package version and reconciliation status.
  • Capacity screens show purchased rights separately from selected active configuration and recommendation.
  • Privileged actions show approval state and second-approver requirement before execution.

docs.title: Product & Scope
docs.text: The LMS is a reusable enterprise control plane for current and future AI products. It centralizes customer/site/device management, licensing, entitlement pools, Marketplace/OTA, model lifecycle, capacity planning, renewal, audit and offline operations.
