docs.title: Consolidated Business Rules
docs.text: This page is the normative cross-domain business-rule checklist for LMS. More detailed pages remain authoritative for implementation specifics.

docs.title: Licensing and entitlement
docs.text:
• Registration, commercial licensing and capacity validation are separate states.
  • Entitlement = what the customer owns; allocation = distribution of pooled rights; grant = device-bound signed executable authorization.
  • Customer pooled quantity must never be over-allocated.
  • Reallocation creates superseding grants and must not allow old/new quantities to remain simultaneously usable indefinitely.
  • Subscription and perpetual base licenses are supported.
  • Subscription add-ons co-terminate with the base by default; explicitly independent add-ons may have their own term.
  • A perpetual base may carry subscription add-ons.
  • Dependent add-ons become dormant when the required base is inactive.
  • Commercial expiry, offline authorization freshness and grace are three independent clocks.
  • Successful check-in never extends commercial expiry.
  • Payment/renewal approval alone does not renew an offline device until it receives and accepts the new signed grant revision.

docs.title: Trials
docs.text:
• Default trial duration is 7 days and is policy-configurable.
  • Trial starts on first successful feature activation, not on request, issuance or package import.
  • Baseline eligibility is one trial per customer entitlement + feature, unless an auditable admin/campaign override permits another trial.
  • A trial is a signed time-limited grant; globally reusable trial licenses are prohibited.

docs.title: Device lifecycle
docs.text:
• Device identity is cryptographic key + versioned weighted hardware fingerprint; MAC is evidence only.
  • Minor hardware changes trigger re-evaluation and normally continue.
  • Major identity changes enter REHOST_REQUIRED; they do not silently destroy or transfer licenses.
  • Decommission/replacement returns eligible allocation to the entitlement pool after approval/reconciliation.
  • Device transfer is request/approval/audit driven; ownership is never silently overwritten.
  • Air-gapped revocation becomes effective only after signed state is imported or existing offline authorization expires.

docs.title: Capacity
docs.text:
• Central capacity assessment is advisory/pre-assessment; local capacity check is authoritative for actual activation.
  • Commercial rights are never silently reduced because hardware is insufficient.
  • Capacity engine recommends alternatives; an operator/customer chooses the allowed configuration.

docs.title: Marketplace and OTA
docs.text:
• Marketplace discovery/trial/purchase does not itself authorize execution.
  • A feature activates only when compatible, licensed, installed, healthy and capacity-validated.
  • Automatic production updates consume Stable by default.
  • LTS deployment is explicitly company-controlled.
  • Normal site releases must automate migration, health-check and rollback; no manual migration step.
  • Models are independently versioned, encrypted, signed and inventory-aware.
  • Offline bundles should contain only missing/required artifacts where possible.

docs.title: Governance
docs.text:
• High-risk actions use maker-checker approval.
  • Audit retention baseline is configurable 1–3 years.
  • Portal + email are initial notification channels; webhook delivery remains extensible.
  • LMS is not an accounting system; ERP integration is separate.

docs.title: Approved Decisions
docs.text: Decision Baseline Backend Python 3.12 + FastAPI modular monolith Database PostgreSQL + SQLAlchemy + Alembic Admin UI React + Vite + TypeScript Deployment SaaS and customer-hosted OS Ubuntu/Linux first; future Windows-compatible abstractions Development auth Username/password; production IAM later ADR Trial Default 7 days, configurable; starts at first successful feature activation Offline validity Default 7 days, hierarchical override Grace Default 7 days, independently configurable Add-ons Normally co-terminate with subscription base Capacity Recommend; never silently alter purchased rights Packaging Traditional signed release bundles; no Docker dependency Auto OTA Supported; Stable channel by default Maintenance window Default 01:00–03:00; customer configurable Rollback Keep 2–3 known-good versions where disk permits Model OTA Independent, encrypted, signed and rollback-capable Audit retention Configurable; baseline 1–3 years ERP Separate system with synchronization interfaces

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
1. One common licensing platform for multiple product families.
  2. Same codebase for SaaS and customer-hosted deployment.
  3. Connected, intermittently connected and fully air-gapped operation.
  4. Highly customized licensing without hard-coded feature columns.
  5. Entitlement pooling with device-specific allocations and grants.
  6. Hardware capability and combined-workload validation before activation.
  7. Trial, purchase, add-on and renewal flows in one platform.
  8. Traditional package OTA plus independent encrypted model OTA.
  9. Automatic/manual update policies, maintenance windows and rollback.
  10. Corporate-grade audit, approval and security controls.

docs.title: Phase 1 non-goals
docs.text:
• Full ERP/accounting capability.
  • Windows-first implementation.
  • Automatic customer-hosted LMS self-upgrade.
  • Premature microservice decomposition.
  • Claiming complete tamper resistance on a root-compromised edge host.

docs.title: Terminology
docs.text: Term Meaning Entitlement Central commercial right purchased or granted to a customer. Entitlement Pool Quantity/rights available to a customer for allocation. Allocation Distribution of pooled rights to devices/sites. Grant Signed, device-bound executable permission derived from entitlement and policy. Trial Grant Time-limited signed grant; default 7 days unless overridden. Offline Validity Time a device may continue without authorized sync/check-in. Grace Restricted period after commercial expiry or policy condition. Release Versioned application/feature/UI/runtime package metadata. Model Release Independently versioned encrypted AI model artifact. Release Set Coherent application, feature, UI, runtime and model snapshot for deployment/rollback. Capacity Assessment Combined workload feasibility evaluation using inventory and benchmark evidence.

docs.title: Acceptance Criteria by Delivery Phase
docs.text: These are minimum exit criteria for phase completion; detailed stories may add stricter criteria.

docs.title: Phase 1 — Trust foundation
docs.text:
• device generates/loads protected key pair
  • enrollment rejects invalid/reused authorization
  • signed grant verifies offline
  • wrong-device/tampered/expired/stale-revision grants are rejected
  • last-known-time rollback scenario is covered by tests
  • audit events exist for enrollment and issuance

docs.title: Phase 2 — Registry & licensing
docs.text:
• customer/site/device topology supports multi-site server assignment
  • entitlement pool cannot be over-allocated
  • reallocations supersede affected device grants
  • base/add-on dependency works
  • subscription and perpetual terms represented without schema change
  • decommission returns rights to pool

docs.title: Phase 3 — Capacity
docs.text:
• stable inventory separated from resource snapshots
  • benchmark profile/version recorded in assessment
  • combined existing+proposed workload evaluated
  • warning/fail produces recommendations
  • commercial quantity remains unchanged on capacity failure

docs.title: Phase 4 — Marketplace & release management
docs.text:
• marketplace hides/disables ineligible actions with reason
  • trial duration can be configured
  • trial starts only after successful activation
  • Stable/LTS channel rules enforced
  • release manifest is immutable and signed
  • unsupported dependency/OS/runtime is blocked

docs.title: Phase 5 — Model OTA & deployment
docs.text:
• installed model inventory prevents unnecessary redownload
  • encrypted model cannot be used without authorization
  • model-only OTA supported
  • automatic/manual modes supported
  • default maintenance window 01:00–03:00 and override works
  • failed health check restores previous coherent release set

docs.title: Phase 6 — Lifecycle
docs.text:
• commercial expiry, offline validity and grace behave independently
  • check-in does not extend commercial term
  • offline renewal can be imported and reconciled
  • revocation behavior is correct for online and air-gapped cases
  • major identity change triggers rehost flow

docs.title: Phase 7 — Hardening
docs.text:
• backup restore successfully rehearsed
  • VAPT findings triaged/remediated per release policy
  • tenant-isolation tests pass
  • monitoring/alerts cover critical workflows
  • operational and support runbooks reviewed
  • production readiness checklist signed off

docs.title: Minimum automation expectation
docs.text: Critical-path API and edge verification tests run in CI. Upgrade/rollback, offline bundle, migration and hardware-capacity scenarios run in dedicated integration/system environments with representative fixtures.

docs.title: Definition of Ready / Definition of Done
Definition of Ready
docs.text: A story/epic is Ready when: - business outcome and acceptance criteria are written - affected actors/scopes are known - state transition is defined - API/data ownership is identified - authorization and tenant boundary are defined - online/offline behaviour is explicit - error/recovery path is documented - security/capacity impact is classified - dependencies and migration needs are known - test approach is identified

docs.title: Definition of Done
docs.text: A change is Done when: - implementation is merged through review - unit/integration/contract tests pass - tenant authorization tests exist where applicable - audit and observability are implemented - DB/API compatibility and migration are validated - upgrade and rollback are tested where applicable - threat/security review is complete - documentation and ADRs are updated in the same PR - acceptance criteria are demonstrated - no unresolved Sev-1/Sev-2 defects remain for release scope

docs.title: Performance, Load & Resilience Testing
docs.text: Functional correctness alone is insufficient for production readiness.

docs.title: Central LMS tests
docs.text:
• API latency under expected and peak concurrency
  • entitlement/allocation transaction contention
  • signing throughput and degraded signing-provider behavior
  • deployment orchestration at fleet scale
  • background-job backlog/recovery
  • artifact metadata operations
  • audit-event volume
  • tenant-isolation under concurrent load

docs.title: Edge tests
docs.text:
• steady-state analytics with licensed maximum workload
  • combined feature workloads
  • update while under normal workload
  • model switch/warm-up
  • low disk/memory conditions
  • service restart/power interruption during install
  • rollback under failure
  • long offline duration within policy

docs.title: Soak tests
docs.text: Long-running tests detect memory leaks, queue growth, resource drift, thermal throttling and repeated check-in/telemetry behavior.

docs.title: Fault injection
docs.text: Exercise recoverable failures such as DB reconnect, artifact-store timeout, signing-service outage, network loss, corrupted package, process crash and interrupted offline import.

docs.title: Exit evidence
docs.text: Record environment, versions, load model, thresholds, measured p50/p95/p99, error rate, recovery behavior and known limits. Performance regressions against approved baseline are release-blocking when they violate product/SLO targets.

docs.title: Release Readiness
docs.text:
• Requirements accepted
  • ADR impact reviewed
  • Code review complete
  • Unit/integration tests green
  • DB migration tested
  • Upgrade from supported prior release tested
  • Rollback tested
  • Package/model signatures validated
  • Capacity metadata reviewed
  • Security scans complete
  • VAPT requirements satisfied
  • Release notes complete
  • Stable/LTS approval recorded

docs.title: Test Strategy
docs.text: Testing follows risk and trust boundaries, not only code modules. Critical licensing/security/update behavior requires automated negative tests and end-to-end evidence.

docs.title: Unit
docs.text: Policy resolution, constraints, grant canonicalization, state transitions, compatibility rules, recommendation logic and error mapping.

docs.title: Repository/database
docs.text: FK/unique/check constraints, tenant-scoped query behavior, transaction rollback, optimistic concurrency, idempotency, migrations and indexes.

docs.title: API integration
docs.text: Authentication, authorization, validation, error envelopes, idempotency and cross-module workflows against real PostgreSQL.

docs.title: Central-edge contract
docs.text: Grant/manifest schemas, signature/canonicalization compatibility, offline request/response, check-in/receipt and release-set contracts.

docs.title: System/end-to-end
docs.text: Registration -> entitlement -> allocation -> grant -> local verification -> install/activation -> receipt; trial, renewal, reallocation, OTA/model OTA, rehost, transfer, revocation and offline flows.

docs.title: Security
docs.text: Tenant isolation, IDOR/BOLA, auth abuse/rate limit, signature tamper, replay/rollback, malformed archive, path traversal, unknown critical schema, key rotation/trust-store and privilege escalation.

docs.title: Capacity/performance
docs.text: Benchmark profile regression, combined workload, stale assessment triggers, representative hardware, local authoritative checks, soak/load/fault tests.

docs.title: Environments
docs.text:
• local/unit with synthetic fixtures
  • integration with PostgreSQL and development signing provider
  • QA with central + edge simulator/representative agents
  • hardware lab for capacity/update/device identity
  • staging production-like environment without uncontrolled production data

docs.title: Test data
docs.text: Use synthetic customers/devices/entitlements and generated test keys. Production private keys/customer exports are prohibited in normal test environments.

docs.title: Automation gates
docs.text: PR CI runs unit, API/integration, migration, tenant isolation, signature/contract and static security tests appropriate to the change. Longer hardware/upgrade/rollback/soak tests run in dedicated pipelines before Stable promotion.

docs.title: Failure injection
docs.text: Required scenarios include signing outage, artifact timeout, DB reconnect, worker restart, duplicate request, process crash during install, power/interruption simulation, corrupted offline bundle and rollback failure.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text: Release evidence links test versions/environment, pass/fail summary, known exceptions and relevant artifacts/logs. A green unit suite alone is not production readiness.

docs.title: Security Architecture
docs.text: Security is a cross-cutting architecture concern, not a release checklist. The LMS security model protects commercial rights, customer isolation, device trust, software/model integrity and recoverability across connected and air-gapped deployments.

docs.title: Security objectives
docs.text:
1. Only authorized humans and registered devices may interact with LMS.
  2. A valid commercial entitlement alone is not enough to execute a feature; the device must hold a valid signed grant.
  3. License/grant issuance must be impossible without the protected signing boundary.
  4. Software/model artifacts must be authenticated before install or decryption.
  5. Cross-customer data access is treated as a security-critical failure.
  6. Offline packages must remain safe when moved through untrusted media/relay systems.
  7. Device-local enforcement must resist replay/rollback and fail closed for unauthorized analytics.
  8. Recovery must remain possible without placing production signing keys in normal backups.
  9. Security controls must remain operable in SaaS and customer-hosted deployments.

docs.title: Security domains
docs.text: Domain Primary controls Human identity OIDC/SSO target, MFA for privileged access, session controls, break-glass governance Device identity device-generated asymmetric key, enrollment authorization, versioned hardware fingerprint Authorization deny-by-default RBAC, tenant/customer/site/device scope, maker-checker Grant trust deterministic canonicalization, isolated license signing, revision/supersession, anti-rollback Release trust separate release signing key, immutable manifest, artifact hash/signature Model protection encrypted model artifact, envelope encryption, device/deployment-authorized key wrapping Data protection TLS, encryption at rest where supported, secret separation, backup encryption Offline trust signed request/response, nonce/request binding, anti-replay, bounded/quarantined package parsing Edge enforcement protected local key/state, runtime authorization, trusted time, quantity enforcement Tenant isolation scope propagation, ownership validation, negative isolation tests Supply chain PR review, SAST/SCA/secret scan, SBOM, build provenance, signed releases Detection/response security audit events, alerts, incident playbooks, evidence preservation

docs.title: Trust model
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    U[Human User] -->|OIDC/password during bootstrap| API[LMS API]
    D[Device Identity Key] -->|signed enrollment/check-in| API
    API -->|authorized signing request| LS[License Signing Boundary]
    API -->|authorized release signing request| RS[Release Signing Boundary]
    API --> DB[(PostgreSQL)]
    API --> AR[(Artifact Repository)]
    AR --> EDGE[Edge Update Manager]
    LS --> EDGE
    RS --> EDGE
    EDGE --> LA[License Agent]
    LA --> RT[Protected Analytics Runtime]

The LMS application never possesses raw production signing private keys.

docs.title: Security decision precedence
docs.text:
1. Approved security ADRs.
  2. Security control baseline.
  3. Product/business policy where it does not weaken non-relaxable controls.
  4. Deployment-specific configuration.

Customer/device overrides cannot weaken a control explicitly marked non-relaxable.

docs.title: Known boundary
docs.text: A root/administrator-compromised edge host cannot be made fully tamper-proof in software alone. LMS therefore focuses on cryptographic authorization, protected local state where practical, integrity verification, auditability and bounded offline authorization rather than claiming impossible absolute protection.

docs.text: Action Minimum role Second approval Audit View customer/device state Support / Customer Admin scoped No access/security log Allocate within approved entitlement pool Customer/Vendor Admin scoped Normally no Yes Increase/create exceptional entitlement Product/Commercial Admin Yes unless approved ERP automation Yes Issue exceptional perpetual/custom grant Product Admin Yes Yes Extend/repeat trial beyond policy Product Admin Yes when outside approved campaign Yes Rehost after motherboard/device-key change Support/Admin Yes Yes Cross-customer device transfer Privileged Admin Yes Yes Publish Development/QA release Developer/Release Manager No Yes Promote Stable Release Manager QA/Security gate according to policy Yes Designate/promote LTS Release Manager Yes Yes Force broad rollout outside normal policy Release Manager/Privileged Admin Yes Yes Override capacity warning/fail where allowed Privileged Admin Yes Yes Override security block Security/Privileged Admin Yes Yes Rotate/activate signing key Security/DevOps Yes Yes Change edge trust bundle/revoke verification key Security/Release Yes Yes Change model KEK/key-wrapping configuration Security/DevOps Yes Yes Revoke individual grant/device Admin/Support policy High-impact cases yes Yes Mass revoke/suspend customer/fleet Vendor/Security Admin Yes Yes Export global audit/security data Auditor/Security/Admin Policy-dependent Yes Use break-glass access Designated emergency role Post-use review; second control where feasible Mandatory

docs.title: Principles
docs.text:
• requester and approver must be distinct when maker-checker is required
  • approval binds to object revision/payload so approved data cannot be silently changed before execution
  • expired/rejected/cancelled approvals cannot execute
  • high-risk automation must preserve equivalent evidence and policy checks
  • development roles remain restricted to non-production release channels by default

docs.title: Edge Host Hardening Baseline
docs.text: Edge controls assume the device may be intermittently connected and physically accessible. The goal is to reduce attack surface and protect legitimate operation; software alone cannot guarantee security against an attacker with persistent root/administrator control.

docs.title: Service isolation
docs.text:
• run LMS edge agents/runtime as dedicated least-privilege service accounts where practical
  • restrict writable directories
  • separate update staging from active runtime paths
  • local management APIs bind to loopback/local IPC by default
  • firewall/network exposure is minimal and documented

docs.title: Key/state storage
docs.text:
• device private key uses TPM/secure element/OS keystore where available; otherwise strongest practical protected filesystem/keyring
  • grant anti-rollback state and trusted time are stored with integrity protection where feasible
  • normal users cannot modify active grant/release state
  • backup/export processes do not copy raw private keys by default

docs.title: Update execution
docs.text:
• signature/hash verification before install
  • install scripts are signed artifacts referenced by manifest
  • scripts run with only required privilege
  • staging directory is non-authoritative until health check commits
  • rollback restores coherent known-good app/model/config state

docs.title: Logging
docs.text: Edge logs avoid secrets and decrypted model data. Security-relevant failures include safe reason code, key ID/trust-bundle version and request/package identifiers.

docs.title: Host maintenance
docs.text: Supported OS/runtime versions and security-patch expectations are part of compatibility policy. Unsupported/vulnerable runtime dependencies may block future releases according to product/security policy.

docs.title: Physical/root compromise limitation
docs.text: An attacker with root may observe runtime memory or alter binaries outside the intended trust model. Cryptographic signing prevents legitimate software from accepting forged central authorization, but it cannot prove a hostile root-owned host is executing unmodified code without additional hardware attestation.

docs.title: Human Identity, Session & Privileged Access Security
docs.text: Development username/password auth is a bootstrap implementation. Production human identity remains an open ADR, but the authorization and session control baseline is defined now.

docs.title: Production target
docs.text:
• OIDC/SSO adapter for enterprise identity providers
  • MFA for privileged/vendor administration where supported
  • role mapping that does not grant global privilege by default
  • explicit logout/revocation and session expiry
  • audit of login success/failure and privileged authentication events

docs.title: Bootstrap/local password mode
docs.text: Where username/password mode is permitted: - adaptive password hashing (Argon2id or approved equivalent) - minimum password policy enforced by deployment/security profile - rate limiting and progressive abuse protection - no plaintext/reversible password storage - password reset tokens are short-lived, single-use and securely random - reset does not reveal whether arbitrary accounts exist

docs.title: Session/token baseline
docs.text:
• short-lived access token/session
  • refresh/session rotation when applicable
  • server-side revocation capability for privileged sessions
  • audience/issuer validation for external IdP tokens
  • clock-skew tolerance is bounded
  • tokens never accepted from query strings
  • token/session identifiers redacted from logs

docs.title: Privileged access
docs.text:
• global/vendor privileged roles granted explicitly
  • periodic access review
  • privilege elevation/role changes generate audit events
  • sensitive actions may require fresh authentication or second approval
  • support access remains customer-scoped unless explicitly elevated

docs.title: Break-glass
docs.text: Emergency access is separate from normal administration, tightly limited, auditable, time-bounded and reviewed after use. Break-glass credentials/tokens are not shared in normal documentation or chat systems.

docs.title: Device versus human identity
docs.text: Human sessions and device cryptographic identity are separate security principals. Human login credentials are never used as the device's long-lived identity.

docs.title: Assisted-Offline Relay Security
docs.text: The relay workstation/laptop is a transport convenience, never a licensing authority.

docs.title: Required properties
docs.text:
• no license or release signing private keys
  • short-lived/operator-scoped authentication to the central LMS where connectivity exists
  • encrypted local storage for staged request/response packages where feasible
  • automatic cleanup/retention policy for staged packages
  • no universal customer/device secrets
  • package integrity preserved end-to-end; relay cannot modify signed content undetected
  • audit of upload/download operator and request ID where possible

docs.title: Lost or compromised relay
docs.text: Compromise of the relay should expose at most staged encrypted/signed package material and short-lived credentials, not signing authority. Replayed/stolen response packages remain bound to request ID, nonce and device identity.

docs.title: Secret categories
docs.text:
• database credentials
  • SMTP/webhook/integration credentials
  • OIDC client secrets where applicable
  • artifact-storage credentials
  • KMS/HSM/signing service authentication
  • telemetry/export credentials
  • internal service tokens

Signing private keys and model KEKs are not ordinary application secrets; they remain inside the protected cryptographic provider.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text: Production secrets are injected from approved secret-management/deployment mechanisms, not committed in source, baked into images/packages or stored in documentation.

docs.title: Rotation
docs.text: Every production secret type has an owner and rotation/revocation procedure. Applications should support overlap where needed so rotation does not require service outage.

docs.title: Certificate lifecycle
docs.text:
• certificates have tracked owner and expiry
  • automated renewal preferred where deployment allows
  • certificate validation never disabled in production
  • hostname/SAN validation required
  • expired/revoked certificate failures alert operations
  • private certificate keys receive restricted filesystem/secret-store permissions

docs.title: Service credentials
docs.text: Use separate credentials by environment and service. Avoid one shared superuser credential across LMS, workers and integrations.

docs.title: Compromise response
docs.text: Suspected secret leakage triggers revocation/rotation, impact review, log/audit search, dependent credential rotation where necessary and incident documentation.

docs.title: Secure Coding Standard
docs.text: This standard applies to backend, portal, edge agents, update tooling, offline package parsers and administrative utilities.

docs.title: Input validation
docs.text:
• treat API, ERP, device, file, manifest and offline-package input as untrusted
  • validate type, length, range, enum, encoding and cross-field invariants
  • define maximum body/upload/archive sizes
  • reject unknown security-critical fields in canonical signed payload formats
  • prevent mass-assignment of protected fields
  • do not trust client-provided tenant/role/status fields

docs.title: File/archive/package handling
docs.text:
• extract only into a dedicated staging directory
  • normalize and validate every path before write
  • reject traversal, absolute paths, device paths and symlink/hardlink escapes
  • cap expanded bytes, file count, nesting depth and compression ratio
  • reject unsigned/unreferenced executable scripts
  • verify manifest signature and hashes before install
  • never execute directly from upload/temp location
  • clean failed/quarantined content according to policy

docs.title: Authentication and authorization
docs.text:
• authenticate before authorization
  • enforce permission + object scope at business-service boundary
  • deny by default
  • never rely on hidden buttons/routes for security
  • prevent IDOR/BOLA by ownership validation for every object reference
  • service/background identities use least privilege
  • privileged reprocessing/override operations are separately authorized

docs.title: Database
docs.text:
• parameterized ORM/query use
  • no string-concatenated SQL with untrusted input
  • explicit transaction boundaries
  • optimistic concurrency for mutable aggregates
  • tenant predicates/ownership joins are mandatory
  • DB errors are mapped to safe application errors
  • migrations reviewed for locking/data-loss implications

docs.title: API and web security
docs.text:
• strict content type
  • secure headers
  • CSRF protection for cookie-based state changes
  • CORS allowlist
  • rate limits for abuse-prone endpoints
  • pagination/bounds on expensive queries
  • request correlation ID
  • avoid reflecting untrusted HTML/script content
  • protect download/export endpoints with the same authorization as source records

docs.title: Cryptography
docs.text:
• approved library/provider only
  • no home-grown crypto
  • CSPRNG for tokens/nonces/keys
  • use library-provided safe secret/token comparison primitives
  • signature verification fails closed
  • explicit algorithm/key ID/canonicalization version
  • never reuse signing keys for unrelated purposes

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text:
• never return stack traces, SQL errors, secret values or internal filesystem paths to clients
  • security-sensitive errors may be externally generalized
  • secure logs retain investigation correlation
  • retryability is explicit

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
Allowed: request ID, safe actor/object IDs, action/result, error code and timings.

Forbidden in normal logs: passwords, bearer/refresh tokens, enrollment secrets, private keys, unwrapped DEKs, decrypted model bytes and sensitive raw signed payloads.

docs.title: Concurrency and idempotency
docs.text: Security-sensitive writes use idempotency and/or optimistic revision checks where duplicate or replay execution would be dangerous.

docs.title: Dependency use
docs.text:
• pin/constraint production dependencies
  • review purpose/maintenance posture of new high-risk dependencies
  • SCA in CI
  • remove unused dependencies
  • never dynamically download and execute code from untrusted locations in production

docs.title: Required negative tests
docs.text: Parser/authz/crypto boundaries include tests for tampered signature, wrong tenant, wrong device, stale revision, replayed nonce, malformed archive, traversal path, oversized input and unknown critical schema fields.

docs.title: Security Control Baseline
docs.text: This is the minimum production security baseline. Customer or regulatory requirements may add controls, but deployment configuration must not silently weaken the non-relaxable requirements below.

docs.title: Human identity and privileged access
docs.text:
• deny-by-default authorization
  • unique human accounts; no shared administrator credentials
  • production target: OIDC/SSO integration
  • MFA required for privileged/vendor administration where the chosen IdP supports it
  • short-lived sessions/tokens with revocation
  • privileged role assignment/removal is audited
  • dormant/terminated account access is revoked promptly
  • emergency/break-glass access is separately controlled, time-bounded and reviewed
  • periodic access review for global/vendor privileged roles

docs.title: Device authentication
docs.text:
• device generates/holds its own asymmetric key pair
  • enrollment authorization is high-entropy, short-lived and single-use
  • central registry stores public key/key ID and fingerprint evidence
  • MAC address is never sufficient identity
  • requests that change sensitive device state are authenticated by registered device identity or an explicitly defined secure bootstrap flow
  • major device-key/identity changes require rehost/re-enrollment approval

docs.title: Authorization
docs.text:
• permission + scope evaluation at service/use-case boundary
  • customer/site/device ownership validated server-side
  • support/global permissions are explicit; no implicit tenant bypass
  • maker-checker for sensitive actions
  • authorization is never UI-only
  • background jobs and asynchronous messages carry tenant scope

docs.title: Network and transport
docs.text:
• TLS for external production HTTP/API traffic
  • approved modern TLS versions/cipher policy set by deployment baseline
  • certificate validation is mandatory; insecure verification bypasses are prohibited
  • internal service endpoints are bound to least-exposed interfaces
  • local-only edge APIs are not externally reachable by default
  • production admin interfaces should be restricted by network policy where deployable

docs.title: Application security
docs.text:
• strict request/file input validation
  • bounded archive/package extraction
  • path traversal, symlink escape and archive-bomb protection
  • MIME/file-type and manifest allowlisting for uploaded artifacts
  • CSRF controls when cookie authentication is used
  • CORS restricted to approved origins
  • secure portal headers
  • rate limiting for authentication, enrollment and import abuse surfaces
  • safe deserialization; no execution of unsigned inline commands
  • SSRF-sensitive integrations use destination allowlists where applicable

docs.title: Secrets management
docs.text:
• secrets are never committed to source control
  • production secrets come from an approved secret manager/KMS/deployment secret store
  • secrets are scoped per environment and service
  • credentials support rotation without code changes
  • secret values are redacted from logs/errors
  • database/service credentials use least privilege
  • development/test credentials are never valid in production

docs.title: Data protection
docs.text:
• encrypted backups
  • database and artifact storage encryption at rest where supported by platform/deployment
  • model artifacts encrypted in storage/distribution
  • highly restricted key material is stored only in protected key systems
  • sensitive exports are authorization-scoped and auditable
  • no passwords, raw auth tokens, private keys, model content keys or decrypted models in normal logs

docs.title: Signing and cryptography
docs.text:
• separate license-signing and release-signing key purposes
  • production key custody through KMS/HSM/equivalent protected service
  • key ID and algorithm recorded in signed objects
  • deterministic canonicalization
  • signature verification fails closed
  • trust-store/key rotation is versioned and tested
  • compromise recovery is documented before production
  • use approved crypto libraries; no custom cryptographic primitives

docs.title: Offline package security
docs.text:
• device-signed canonical request
  • request ID + nonce + expiry + device binding
  • central replay/idempotency checks
  • response bound to originating request/device
  • signatures verified before processing executable/decryptable content
  • package import performed in staging/quarantine area
  • bounded file count/size/path
  • unknown executable content rejected
  • signed receipt generated after accepted activation/install

docs.title: Edge local security
docs.text:
• device private key stored using strongest practical platform protection
  • monotonic accepted grant revision persisted
  • last-known trusted time persisted
  • product runtime checks authorization at execution boundaries
  • update installation runs with least privilege practical for platform
  • rollback state protected from untrusted package content
  • local APIs bind to loopback/local IPC unless explicitly required otherwise

docs.title: Secure SDLC
docs.text: Threat review -> code review -> unit/integration/security tests -> SAST/SCA/secret scan -> package/provenance checks -> QA -> VAPT where required -> remediation/disposition -> release approval.

docs.title: Non-relaxable controls
docs.text: The following cannot be disabled by customer/site/device policy: signature verification, tenant authorization, private-key separation, anti-replay binding for offline packages, production secret isolation, audit of privileged actions and rejection of invalid/tampered signed content.

docs.title: Security Logging, Detection & Alerting
docs.text: Security logging is separate from high-volume product telemetry. Security events must be durable enough for investigation and customer/tenant scoping.

docs.title: Required security event families
docs.text:
• login success/failure and lock/rate-limit events
  • privileged role assignment/removal
  • maker-checker request/approval/rejection
  • enrollment authorization creation/use/replay failure
  • device key registration/rehost/transfer
  • grant issue/revoke/supersession/verification failure
  • signing request/key rotation/trust-bundle change
  • artifact/model signature/hash failure
  • offline import rejection/replay/path/archive security failure
  • tenant authorization denial and suspected cross-tenant access
  • capacity/security override
  • release Stable/LTS promotion and forced rollout
  • secret/certificate rotation administrative actions
  • audit export and sensitive report access

docs.title: Event fields
docs.text:
Security events record event type/version, UTC timestamp, request/correlation ID, actor principal/type, tenant/customer scope, source/device identifier where safe, target object, action/result, stable reason/error code and approval reference where relevant.

Secrets, raw bearer tokens, private keys, plaintext DEKs and decrypted models are prohibited from security logs.

docs.title: Detection examples
docs.text: Signal Detection/alert intent repeated enrollment-token failures brute-force/abuse investigation cross-tenant authorization denials spike tenant isolation/security investigation unknown signing key ID at devices trust-bundle/deployment or compromise investigation repeated offline replay rejection operational misuse or malicious replay signature/hash failures across fleet artifact/signing/repository incident privileged override volume anomaly governance/security review signing API denial/failure anomaly signing-service incident

docs.title: Retention and access
docs.text: Security/audit retention follows configured policy with a baseline of 1–3 years. Access to global security logs is restricted and audited; customer-visible audit views are tenant-scoped.

docs.title: Time and integrity
docs.text: Central systems use reliable time synchronization. Audit/security records are append-only at the application level; any archival/export pipeline preserves event identity and ordering metadata.

docs.title: Incident linkage
docs.text: Alerts and incidents should carry request/event identifiers that allow responders to trace from portal/API action through business audit event, signing/deployment job and edge receipt without exposing sensitive payloads.

docs.title: Signing Key Rotation & Recovery
docs.text: License-signing and release-signing keys have separate lifecycle and trust purpose.

docs.title: Key states
docs.text:
GENERATED -> ACTIVE -> RETIRING -> RETIRED -> DESTROYED

Compromised keys may enter REVOKED/COMPROMISED through emergency procedure.

docs.title: Rotation
docs.text:
1. Generate new key in protected provider.
  2. Distribute/ship new public verification key or trust bundle before first use.
  3. Mark new key active for signing.
  4. Keep old public key trusted for the planned verification window.
  5. Stop issuing new artifacts with retiring key.
  6. Retire old key after compatible clients have received trust updates.

docs.title: Recovery
docs.text: Private-key recovery uses KMS/HSM/provider-specific protected mechanisms and is separated from normal database backup. Recovery exercises must not export raw private material unless the approved provider procedure explicitly requires a protected escrow mechanism.

docs.title: Compromise response
docs.text:
• stop signing with affected key immediately
  • identify grants/releases signed with the key
  • activate replacement key/trust bundle
  • assess offline devices that may not receive trust updates immediately
  • supersede/revoke affected artifacts where necessary
  • preserve audit evidence and run security incident process

docs.title: Trust-store versioning
docs.text: Edge verification components record trust-store version and key IDs so support can distinguish unknown-key failures from invalid signatures.

docs.title: Key-purpose separation
docs.text:
At minimum, use separate key purposes for:

  1. license/grant signing
  2. application/release manifest signing
  3. model/package signing if separated operationally
  4. model content-encryption key wrapping/master-key operations
  5. device identity keys

A single universal private key must not perform all trust functions.

docs.title: Grant signing flow
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant LMS as LMS Grant Service
    participant POL as Policy/Entitlement
    participant SIG as Protected License Signer
    participant D as Device License Agent
    LMS->>POL: Resolve approved grant payload
    POL-->>LMS: Canonical grant fields
    LMS->>SIG: Authorized signing request + canonical bytes/hash
    SIG-->>LMS: key_id + algorithm + signature
    LMS-->>D: Signed grant
    D->>D: Rebuild canonical bytes and verify signature

The LMS stores signing metadata and signed output; raw signing private key material never enters application/database storage.

docs.title: Release signing
docs.text:
Release and model manifests are immutable after publication. Edge verifies manifest schema/version, release-signing key trust, manifest signature, artifact content hash, artifact signature if the artifact format carries one, and target compatibility.

No package is executed merely because it came from the artifact repository.

docs.title: Cryptographic algorithm baseline
docs.text:
Ed25519 is the preferred initial signature algorithm where required platforms/providers support it. Final algorithm/provider support remains subject to security and compatibility review. SHA-256 or stronger is used for content integrity unless an approved profile replaces it.

Algorithm and canonicalization profile are versioned in signed objects so future migration is possible.

docs.title: Model encryption
docs.text:
Model binaries are encrypted independently from license grants. Entitlement answers whether a device may use a model; the encryption system determines whether an authorized device/deployment can obtain the content key.

Random per-artifact DEK
        ↓ encrypts
Encrypted model artifact
        ↓
DEK wrapped by protected KEK / device-deployment authorization
        ↓
Authorized edge unwrap path

docs.title: Model key handling requirements
docs.text:
• DEKs generated with a CSPRNG
  • plaintext DEKs not stored in normal LMS DB/logs
  • wrapped-key metadata records model release, key version and authorized scope
  • decryption authorization tied to valid device/deployment context
  • plaintext model exposure minimized on edge
  • temporary/cache plaintext handling defined by edge implementation
  • revocation cannot guarantee remote deletion on a hostile fully offline/root-compromised host; it prevents legitimate future authorization/use according to policy

A universal embedded password or customer-wide static decryption secret is prohibited.

docs.title: Trust-store management
docs.text: Devices retain a versioned trust bundle with current and retiring verification public keys. Unknown key ID, invalid signature or revoked trust key is a hard verification failure.

docs.title: Open security decision
docs.text: Exact model key hierarchy, KMS/HSM integration, per-device vs per-deployment key wrapping, local secure-storage facility and rotation cadence remain ADR-009 and must be resolved before production model-key implementation is frozen.

docs.title: Required controls
docs.text:
• source changes through reviewed pull requests
  • protected production release branch/tag process
  • pinned/controlled dependencies
  • SCA/dependency vulnerability scanning
  • SAST and secret scanning
  • build provenance/traceability to source commit
  • SBOM generation for production release packages
  • signed immutable release manifests/artifacts
  • malware/file-type scanning for uploaded artifacts where applicable
  • separation of development signing and production release signing

docs.title: Artifact provenance
docs.text: A production artifact must be traceable to source commit/tag, CI build identity, build environment/version, dependency/SBOM record, test/security evidence, release manifest and signing key ID.

docs.title: Third-party dependencies
docs.text: Critical CVEs are triaged against exploitability and exposure. Approved remediation windows and exception process must be defined by Security/Engineering governance.

docs.title: Build environment
docs.text: Production builds should be reproducible or at minimum controlled and isolated. Build agents must not persist production signing secrets; signing occurs through protected provider integration.

docs.title: Release gate
docs.text: A release with unresolved prohibited-severity supply-chain findings cannot be promoted to Stable/LTS without explicit security disposition.

docs.title: Tenant Isolation Standard
docs.text: SaaS mode is multi-tenant. Cross-tenant disclosure or mutation is treated as a security-critical defect.

docs.title: Enforcement model
docs.text: Every business object is associated with a customer/tenant directly or through a verified ownership path. Authorization resolves caller scope before repository/service operations.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Never accept customer_id as proof of access.
  • Repository methods for tenant data require explicit scope/context.
  • Background jobs carry tenant identity with the job payload.
  • Audit queries are tenant-scoped unless caller has explicit global audit permission.
  • Artifact/deployment targets are validated against customer ownership before delivery.
  • Customer-hosted mode may be single-customer, but code paths remain compatible with tenant checks.

docs.title: Required tests
docs.text:
1. user from Customer A cannot read Customer B object by ID
  2. user from A cannot enumerate B through filters/search
  3. user from A cannot mutate B using guessed IDs
  4. background jobs cannot cross tenant due to missing scope
  5. offline request for one customer cannot obtain another customer's grant/artifact
  6. support/global roles are tested for both allowed and denied scope combinations

Tenant isolation regression tests are release blockers.

docs.title: Threat Model & VAPT
docs.text: Threat Baseline control Enrollment/token guessing High entropy, short-lived/single-use authorization, rate limiting Forged license Protected central signing key + digitally signed grants Tampered package/model Signature + hash + manifest verification MAC spoofing Device cryptographic key + weighted/versioned fingerprint; MAC only evidence Device cloning Device-bound grants, protected local key/state, quantity controls Clock rollback Persist last-known trusted time; suspicious backward jumps cause reject/restrict until revalidation Grant rollback Monotonic revision/sequence and protected local accepted-state Request replay Nonce, request hash, expiry, idempotency, device binding Stolen/compromised relay Transport-only role, short-lived auth, encrypted staging where feasible, no signing authority Tenant escape Strict tenant-scoped authorization and negative isolation tests Update crash Atomic staging, health check, coherent release-set rollback Transfer/rehost abuse Approval, maker-checker for sensitive cases, immutable audit lineage Signing-key compromise Key-purpose separation, rotation/recovery plan, incident procedure Offline revocation delay Accepted design limitation; revoke on signed import or offline expiry Fully compromised/root edge Software signatures/hardening reduce risk but cannot guarantee tamper-proof execution on a hostile root-controlled host

docs.title: VAPT coverage
docs.text:
VAPT/release security validation covers at minimum:

  • enrollment
  • authentication and authorization
  • tenant isolation
  • license/grant issuance
  • signing gateway
  • offline package import/export
  • malformed/archive/path traversal inputs
  • artifact/model upload and verification
  • update execution and rollback
  • replay/rollback
  • transfer/rehost/decommission
  • portal/API privileged actions

High-risk findings must be remediated or explicitly dispositioned before production promotion according to security policy.

docs.title: Sources
docs.text: Vulnerabilities may be identified through SAST, SCA, secret scanning, container/package scanning where applicable, VAPT, customer reports, vendor advisories, CVEs and internal security review.

docs.title: Triage
docs.text: Each finding records severity, exploitability, affected component/version, internet/customer exposure, tenant/security impact, remediation owner and target release.

docs.title: Release policy
docs.text:
• exploitable critical findings affecting auth, tenant isolation, signing, remote code execution or package verification are production release blockers unless Security formally accepts the risk
  • high findings require explicit disposition before Stable/LTS promotion
  • lower findings follow approved remediation timelines

Exact remediation SLAs are an organizational policy decision and should be adopted before production launch.

docs.title: Dependency vulnerabilities
docs.text: Dependency updates are tested for compatibility, migrations and edge/runtime impacts. A version is not upgraded blindly solely because a scanner reports a CVE; exploitability and safe remediation are evaluated, but accepted exceptions remain documented and time-bounded.

docs.title: Disclosure
docs.text: Security reports are routed to an approved private channel. Public disclosure/customer notification follows incident and legal/compliance policy, not ad-hoc engineering communication.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: Remediation requires retest/scanner evidence and, for important manual findings, security verification before closure.

docs.title: Support Error Code Catalogue
docs.text: Stable support codes allow customer support, logs and UI to refer to the same failure without exposing stack traces.

docs.title: Naming format
docs.text:
LMS-<DOMAIN>-<HTTP>-<NNN>

Examples:

Code Meaning Operator action LMS-AUTH-401-001 Invalid credentials Verify account; do not disclose which credential failed LMS-DEVICE-409-001 Device already registered to another active identity Start transfer/rehost investigation LMS-DEVICE-409-002 Rehost required after major identity change Submit rehost approval LMS-ENT-409-001 Entitlement pool over-allocation Reduce requested allocation or increase approved entitlement LMS-GRANT-409-001 Stale grant revision Fetch/import newest grant LMS-GRANT-403-002 Feature not entitled Check entitlement/purchase state LMS-OFFLINE-409-001 Offline response does not match request nonce/device Regenerate from fresh request LMS-OFFLINE-409-002 Offline package replay detected Reject; investigate operator/process LMS-CAP-422-001 Workload incompatible with hardware Review capacity recommendations LMS-CAP-409-002 Capacity assessment based on stale inventory Refresh inventory and reassess LMS-REL-422-001 Release incompatible with OS/runtime Select compatible release LMS-REL-409-002 Release blocked by dependency Resolve required runtime/model LMS-UPD-500-001 Install failed; rollback completed Inspect install logs and health-check failure LMS-UPD-500-002 Install failed; rollback also failed Escalate Sev-2/Sev-1 based on scope LMS-SIGN-503-001 Signing service unavailable Retry later; operations alert required

docs.title: Support policy
docs.text: UI shows the stable code and a customer-safe message. Secure logs retain request ID and technical context. Runbooks map critical codes to diagnostic steps.

docs.title: Telemetry Delivery, Buffering & Retention
docs.text: Telemetry is best-effort operational/analytics data unless a specific event is also persisted transactionally in LMS.

docs.title: Edge delivery
docs.text:
• aggregate where possible before upload
  • batch and compress to reduce bandwidth
  • support bounded local buffering during offline periods
  • retry transient failures with backoff
  • never allow telemetry backlog to consume unbounded disk
  • discard/roll up lowest-value historical telemetry according to policy before affecting core product operation

docs.title: Ordering and deduplication
docs.text: Events carry event ID, device ID and event timestamp. Central ingestion is idempotent where duplicate delivery is possible. Analytics pipelines must tolerate delayed/out-of-order events.

docs.title: Connectivity modes
docs.text: Connected devices may stream/batch periodically. Assisted-offline/air-gapped telemetry export is optional and must be explicitly designed; licensing does not depend on high-volume telemetry being returned.

docs.title: Retention
docs.text: Operational capacity/deployment evidence needed for licensing/support remains in transactional records according to audit/support policy. High-volume telemetry uses a separate retention policy/storage tier.

docs.title: Privacy
docs.text: Do not collect video/image content or personally identifying analytics payloads by default unless separately approved. Telemetry privacy, residency and opt-in/opt-out remain an open product/security decision.

docs.title: Usage Telemetry Schema
docs.text: High-volume telemetry is logically separate from transactional licensing/audit data. Licensing decisions must not depend on best-effort analytics delivery unless a future approved design explicitly says otherwise.

docs.title: Telemetry families
docs.text:
• camera/input usage aggregates
  • feature usage
  • active hours
  • inference counts
  • performance/latency aggregates
  • capacity/resource history
  • trial activity aggregates
  • runtime/application/model versions
  • deployment health aggregates

docs.title: Common event envelope
docs.text:
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "event_id": "tel_...",
  "device_id": "dev_001",
  "customer_id": "cust_001",
  "site_id": "site_a",
  "event_type": "feature_usage_aggregate",
  "occurred_at": "2026-10-18T11:00:00Z",
  "period": {"start": "2026-10-18T10:00:00Z", "end": "2026-10-18T11:00:00Z"},
  "dimensions": {
    "feature_id": "ppe_detection",
    "app_version": "5.8.0",
    "model_version": "7.3.0"
  },
  "metrics": {
    "active_minutes": 55,
    "inference_count": 183240,
    "camera_count": 4
  }
}

docs.title: Schema rules
docs.text:
• version every event family
  • timestamps in UTC
  • event ID for deduplication
  • customer/device/site attribution validated server-side against registered ownership
  • additive evolution preferred; breaking changes create new schema/event version
  • large arbitrary JSON payloads are avoided when stable typed dimensions/metrics exist

docs.title: Operational versus telemetry truth
docs.text: Grant acceptance, installation receipt, entitlement mutation and privileged audit events remain transactional LMS records. Telemetry can copy/aggregate them for analytics but is not the sole source of operational truth.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text: PostgreSQL remains the operational transactional store. High-volume telemetry should use a dedicated time-series/analytics/warehouse path when volume warrants it.

docs.title: Privacy boundary
docs.text: Video/image content and personally identifying analytic payloads are not collected by default. Retention, opt-in/opt-out, residency and allowed customer-specific telemetry remain an explicit open product/security decision.
